Sports.title: Criminal or saviour? Rui Pinto abandoned by Portuguese authorities after Manchester City leaks
Sports.content:
More than a decade after Rui Pinto set up the Football Leaks website in a crusade triggered by the Fifa scandal in 2015, he finds himself in the middle of a growing storm. The former history student with trademark spiky hair who used to make extra cash selling books about the second world war has not held back with his statements on social media since Manchester City’s guilty verdict from an independent Premier League commission.

The first targets for Pinto, whose leaks of private documents prompted first Uefa then the Premier League to investigate City’s financial affairs, were what he alleged were the club’s “cheating” executives for demonstrating “a complete lack of respect for the rules”. On Wednesday he turned his attention to the Fifa president, Gianni Infantino.

Less than two hours later, Portuguese authorities confirmed Pinto would no longer be protected as a witness. That is understood to have come as a surprise to the 37-year-old, who finds himself without a job, a home or an income. He has been living in a safe house under protection and has never disclosed his location, and it is understood he has received no visitors.

The Guardian understands talks had been initiated to begin the process of reintegrating Pinto back into social and professional life. That initiative will be halted, leaving Pinto to fend for himself. He has been advised not to return home, contact family members or visit crowded places socially or for work.

Pinto has been a protected witness since 2020 after he agreed to grant Portuguese authorities access to millions of files acquired before his arrest in Budapest, where he moved after a year in the Hungarian capital as an Erasmus student. He has since become a cause célèbre who divides opinion in his homeland and been compared to Edward Snowden and Julian Assange.

The Premier League’s case against City drew heavily on evidence provided by Football Leaks, including the chief executive, Ferran Soriano, writing in an internal memo: “We will need to fight this and do it in a way that is not visible, or we will be pointed out as the global enemies of football.” City continue to protest their innocence and Soriano said this week the club would appeal on the basis that the commission’s verdict “contains clear, material errors of law, principle and fact and that it is unsafe”.

The question of whether the evidence should be used provoked huge public debate in Portugal, but the Premier League’s regulations stipulate that any investigation “shall not be bound by judicial rules governing the admissibility of evidence. Instead, facts relating to a breach of these rules may be established by any reliable means.”

View image in fullscreen Rui Pinto has been advised not to return home, contact family members or visit crowded places. Composite: Manchester City FC/AFP via Getty Images; Manchester City FC via Getty Images

That tallies with Pinto’s assertion in 2019 that it is “nonsense” to claim the data he provided is tainted because it was obtained illegally. “The documents are authentic,” he said. “That is what matters. This and the content. I don’t consider myself as a hacker, but as a citizen who acted in the public interest. My sole intention was to reveal illicit practices that affect the world of football.”

Pinto wore a bulletproof vest during his first trial in 2020 and came in through a dedicated entrance guarded by special forces. People attending the proceedings were searched three times and not allowed to bring mobile phones or computers into the courtroom. At the start of the trial, snipers were positioned on buildings near the courthouse.

He was given a suspended four-year sentence in September 2023 after being found guilty on counts of attempted extortion, illegal access to data and breach of correspondence. Pinto has always insisted he never received money but has admitted regret over asking Doyen Sports Investments for money after he obtained thousands of the agency’s internal emails.

He said to Der Spiegel in 2019: “I told myself: ‘If I allow them to buy me out now, I am no better than this whole business.’ So, I wrote to Doyen and told them to keep their money. Not a single cent was paid. What I did was very naive. Looking back now, I regret it. But I repeat that I deny having committed any criminal offence.”

That defence was found to be “not credible” by the judge, who said Pinto and his co-defendant, the lawyer Aníbal Pinto, were “well aware of the illegality of their conduct”. Rui Pinto started living in a safe house after being sentenced. He lost his mother to cancer when he was 11 and is permitted to communicate with his father occasionally. Even when he was in a relationship with the actor Mikaela Lupu, who he said he had met over “a glass of wine and a book” when announcing they had split last year, the security of the property was never compromised.

For six years, Pinto has been seen in public only twice. On one of those occasions, at a supermarket in Lisbon, he was accompanied by police officers and wore a cap and sunglasses. On the other, he was assaulted in an altercation believed to have been sparked for football-related reasons. It is understood that Pinto was left with a bruised eyebrow and the police were informed, although no complaint was filed.

The decision to end his witness protection has raised concerns for his welfare. Pinto is understood to fear for his safety. A bounty was reportedly placed on his head after the revelations made by Football Leaks and Luanda Leaks, which exposed the inner workings of the business empire of Africa’s richest woman, Isabel dos Santos. She denied corruption allegations.

The Guardian attempted to obtain clarification from the commission for special security programmes (CPES), a Portuguese body under the ministry of justice responsible for managing special witness protection programmes, as to why Pinto is no longer a protected witness but received no response. There has been speculation it could be a response to Pinto being accused of hacking the computer systems of PLMJ, the Portuguese law firm founded by José Miguel Júdice.

Júdice testified against Pinto during the Football Leaks trial, describing the episode as a theft that had caused him significant moral and psychological distress. Júdice is the father of Rita Alarcão Júdice, Portugal’s minister of justice since June 2025.

In April, Pinto was acquitted in a second trial of 241 counts of illegally accessing email accounts belonging to several Portuguese sports bodies, including Benfica, and to law firms, magistrates and the tax authority. None of the evidence he provided to the Portuguese authorities has resulted in any charges.

Sports.title: Cristiano Ronaldo’s Portugal walkout divides a nation as Jorge Jesus asserts control
Sports.content:
The drama surrounding Cristiano Ronaldo and the national team has naturally become the biggest story here in Portugal. It led Wednesday evening’s news broadcasts and made the front page of virtually every major newspaper. For some, Ronaldo was right to walk out on the squad days after spending half an hour warming up against Norway without being brought on in an apparent provocation by Jorge Jesus. For others, the forward’s behaviour was intolerable and his departure a matter of time, particularly once he found himself face to face with such a strong-minded head coach.

Ronaldo has promised to tell his side of the story soon, and Jesus will speak on Thursday night after the Nations League match in Denmark. A confrontation between these two huge personalities had been simmering in the background. Jesus was inevitably asked in his first press conference with the team in July how his relationship with Ronaldo would work. Jesus, who coached Ronaldo at Al-Nassr, answered categorically.

“Cris will never be a problem for the national team or for me,” he said, insisting he had Ronaldo’s temperament under control. The harmony between coach and player did not last long.

In Portugal, reaction has inevitably split into two camps. In many ways this is a repeat of the debate over Ronaldo’s automatic place in the starting XI at this summer’s World Cup, and Roberto Martínez’s decision to keep the captain on the pitch for the full 90 minutes in all but one of the five matches – despite there being no obvious tactical or physical explanation for it. Even when Ronaldo came off in the last 32 against Croatia, it was not until the 81st minute.

Ronaldo’s fans are firmly behind him, defending him fiercely on social media. Much of the general public, though, feels the player has turned his back on the national team. That was the message splashed in big letters across the front page of O Jogo, one of Portugal’s leading sports newspapers.

Across the Portuguese media, most newspapers and commentators have sided with the view that Ronaldo behaved selfishly. There are, however, some voices – particularly in newspapers and television outlets in which Ronaldo is a shareholder – who have turned their criticism towards Jesus, accusing him of ingratitude and of indefensibly going back on his word.

But what actually caused the controversy? According to Jesus, he and Ronaldo had a verbal agreement that the 41-year-old would not start against Norway last Sunday, three days after he played for 67 minutes against Wales in the coach’s first match, but would come on. During the game, which Portugal won 2-1, those plans changed: Ronaldo remained an unused substitute, Jesus making the decision for tactical reasons. Ronaldo reportedly viewed the incident as a humiliation.

View image in fullscreen Cristiano Ronaldo, pictured in action against DR Congo, played in every Portugal match in the World Cup. Photograph: Ashley Landis/AP

The first signs of the breakdown came immediately after the final whistle when Ronaldo left the pitch and did not join his teammates as they saluted their supporters in Oslo. Ronaldo’s frustration with Jesus reportedly reached astronomical levels during the manager’s press conference on Wednesday.

Asked about keeping Ronaldo on the bench, Jesus asserted absolute control, in essence making clear that Ronaldo did not run the team and would not be able to change or influence the tactics. It was a transparent message to Ronaldo – and to the Portuguese football federation (FPF): the manager is in charge.

“I can promise whatever I want,” the 72-year-old said. “I’m the coach and I told the player that he wasn’t going to play. I told him I would take him to the bench and that, if I needed him for 30 minutes, he would play. But I saw the game differently, so he didn’t come on. It won’t be Cristiano, or any other player, who changes my ideas as a coach. Never. Neither him nor anyone else. Not even a president. Never. Zero.”

Jesus also stated his intention to start Gonçalo Ramos rather than Ronaldo in Monday’s game.

View image in fullscreen Jorge Jesus has struck a defiant tone over Cristiano Ronaldo. ‘It won’t be Cristiano, or any other player, who changes my ideas as a coach,’ he said. Photograph: José Sena Goulão/EPA

What happened next is what everyone has seen. Ronaldo abruptly left the team hotel, boarded a plane and posted on social media, promising to reveal the truth soon.

Some believe there has been a decline in Ronaldo’s communication since he split almost four years ago from the agent Jorge Mendes after giving an interview to Piers Morgan that triggered his departure from Manchester United. The Ronaldo-Mendes friendship and family connection reportedly remain intact, but the player is managed by a team he assembled himself. Some have questioned whether he is surrounded by too many yes-men, without enough people willing or able to tell him when something risks creating a negative image.

Once again, the narrative around Portugal’s national team is dominated by controversy surrounding Ronaldo. He is at risk of an FPF suspension of between one and six months, as well as a fine, for breaching its disciplinary code.

In the absence of both men’s accounts, rumours are spreading like wildfire. Some publications are claiming Ronaldo will never return to the national team. After 234 appearances over the past 23 years and 146 goals, is this how Ronaldo will say goodbye to his country?

Sports.title: Jürgen Klopp disgusted by claims his Germany team are ‘not white enough’
Sports.content:
Jürgen Klopp has reacted with disgust to a social media debate questioning whether the Germany team he is in the process of forming are “white enough”. Klopp said he believed there was no point in giving room to “such people and their utterances”, dismissing them as “complete nonsense”.

Asked to respond to the debate as to whether the national team were “not German enough” or “not white enough”, he said: “There is absolutely no reason to pay attention to these people. You won’t get my thoughts on this. I have little time in everyday life for idiocy – and even less on social media.

“The great crux of our lives is that everyone is allowed to express their opinion … it’s insane when something like that exists.”

Klopp said watching sportspeople interact with each other was proof to him that mutual respect was still possible. “The world could learn a thing or two from a sports changing room … There, everyone is respected based on the facts and not discredited based on false opinions.”

Klopp, whose plans for Germany since he took over as coach in the summer have attracted huge attention, said the players he had gathered at the national team camp, including several players with a migrant background, “could not be better united than they are”.

The barrage of racist and generally offensive commentaries on social media followed Germany’s 1-0 defeat by Greece last Sunday, in the Nations League, marking the first time Greece had beaten Germany.

It is also reflective of plenty of utterances from MPs of the far-right Alternative für Deutschland (AfD), the largest opposition party in the Bundestag, who have repeatedly and consistently criticised the diversity and ethnic makeup of the national team, often referring to the squad in derogatory terms such as a “politically correct mercenary force”.

Sports.title: England forward Ivan Toney pleads not guilty to Soho nightclub assault
Sports.content:
Ivan Toney has pleaded not guilty to assault after being accused of head-butting and punching a member of the public at a Soho nightclub. The England striker appeared at Westminster magistrates court on Thursday, entering a plea of not guilty to assault occasioning actual bodily harm.

The court heard that on 6 December last year, words were exchanged between the 30-year-old striker and Saber Da Silva at 100 Wardour Street, a live music venue. The prosecutor, Tom Heslop, said it was not known what was said between the two men, but the exchange resulted in them “squaring up” to one another before Toney “lunged forward and head-butted the complainant, followed by a few punches”. The altercation left Da Silva with injuries to his nose and fingers, it was alleged.

Quick Guide How do I 

Toney has won 10 caps for England and was part of the squad that reached the Euro 2024 final. He plays for the Saudi Pro League side Al-Ahli and was included in the England squad for the World Cup during the summer, coming on as a substitute in the semi-final defeat by Argentina and starting the third-place playoff win against France.

In a hearing that lasted 12 minutes, Toney was asked by the District Judge, Briony Clarke, if he wanted the case to be heard at magistrates or crown court. He stood and replied: “Crown court.” His trial will take place before a judge and jury.

Toney was released on unconditional bail, but warned by the judge that if he does not attend Southwark crown court at 9.30am on the appointed date, a warrant could be issued for his arrest.

Toney was charged on 31 July after a Metropolitan police investigation. When the charge was announced, a spokesperson for Toney said: “Ivan acknowledges the charge and although he is naturally shocked, he looks forward to being given the opportunity to clear his name in court.”

Toney started his career at his home town club, Northampton. He moved to Newcastle, where he made two league appearances before joining Peterborough. After signing for Brentford, Toney’s goals helped them win promotion to the Premier League in 2021, where he established himself as one of the top-flight’s leading forwards. He moved to Al-Ahli in 2024 for £40m.

Sports.title: US lined up instead of Qatar to host inaugural Women’s Club World Cup
Sports.content:
The US is poised to host the first Women’s Club World Cup in January 2028, becoming the latest in a series of major Fifa tournaments staged in North America. Discussions to take the competition to the US are at an advanced stage, with Los Angeles and San Diego among the favoured host cities.

It will follow the men’s tournament, whose expanded version debuted last year, in being staged by a country that also hosted the men’s World Cup this summer.

While a deal is yet to be confirmed, the path has cleared for the US to hold the 19-team event without going through a formal bidding process, even though Qatar was in talks with Fifa about hosting.

The winter scheduling will avoid a clash with the men’s Copa América, which the US is the frontrunner to host in June and July 2028, but raises the prospect of a hectic year-round calendar for the world’s top players. The Club World Cup is placed squarely between the 2027 Women’s World Cup and the 2028 Olympics, which will demand full-strength squads. A number of top clubs are in favour of a rule change limiting players to one international tournament per year, whether for club or country.

Fifa is keen to use the Club World Cup as a dry run for the 2031 Women’s World Cup, which the US will host in conjunction with Mexico, Costa Rica and Jamaica in a decision to be formally approved at an Extraordinary Fifa Congress on 23 November.

Football’s global body is eager to assess the stadium venues, pricing and demand for tickets at the smaller 19-team Club World Cup before the 48-team World Cup three years later. Time to organise and market the Club World Cup is tight, given it will start on 5 January 2028.

Sources have cited the chaos engulfing Fifa’s leadership since the emergence of Gianni Infantino’s ill-fated FFE scheme as a significant reason for the backlog of hosting decisions still to be taken. In July, Europe’s top clubs threatened not to participate in future Club World Cups unless the FFE project was shelved. They also warned the threat would hold unless a joint venture between European Football Clubs and Fifa, agreed in outline form, but yet to be signed off, was completed before television rights could be sold for the women’s Club World Cup.

Another tournament awaiting a venue is the 2029 men’s Club World Cup. The US has expressed interest in hosting that competition, but should the women’s event be confirmed it appears more likely to be co-hosted by Morocco, Spain and Portugal before they jointly host the men’s World Cup the following year.

Sports.title: Yemen and football in the face of civil war: ‘It would be very nice to give the world a different headline’
Sports.content:
The Yemen national coach, Noureddine Ould Ali, chose not to reach for a good old-fashioned football excuse after his team’s 1-0 loss to Qatar in the Gulf Cup on Saturday, despite a clear penalty not given their way. The defeat meant the Reds crashed out of the eight-team regional tournament, taking place in Jeddah, Saudi Arabia, with a game of the group stage remaining.

There are other factors the Algerian could list for a defeat against a team that was at the World Cup. Qatar have the Aspire Academy, state of the art stadiums and a former Spain and Real Madrid coach – Julen Lopetegui – in charge. Yemen have nothing approaching that and have not played a home game since 2012, a 2-1 win over Palestine in Sanaa.

Two years later, the capital city came under the control of the Houthis, an Iran-backed militant group, provoking a Saudi-led intervention and years of fighting. The United Nations brokered a truce in 2022 that did reduce hostilities, but the situation has escalated again. In early September, the Houthis swept down the Red Sea coast in its first major military advance in five years and have been targeting Riyadh and other places in Saudi Arabia with missile strikes.

View image in fullscreen Yemen will play in the Asian Cup in January for the second time, managing to qualify despite political turmoil in their country. Photograph: Sipa US/Alamy Live News

At the time, the national team had been training in the southern port city of Aden, home of the presidential leadership council, Yemen’s internationally recognised, Saudi-backed, governing body. “The situation in Aden was OK. We tried our best and had a training camp with local players and then we joined up with the rest of the squad in Jeddah,” Ould Ali says.

“The situation is a political situation and it is not stable. In football we have to be careful. We have a lot of attention on outside factors, but we always try to focus on the football and do better. In Saudi Arabia, the welcome has been great, the people are very friendly and there is a high level of training facilities, hotels and everything. It means we could focus on football.”

Losing 4-0 to the United Arab Emirates in the opener was a reality check, but the UAE have a lot of naturalised talent from overseas to count on and even Andrés Iniesta coaching in the domestic second tier. Yemen barely has a top tier with the local league affected by the fighting. They still beat Bahrain 5-2 in their final group game.

“The league stopped for a long time and restarted this year and they finished the first half of the season,” Ould Ali says. “It is very important. The players need to play, need to keep fit and show their talent.

“The people support us. It is a religion in Yemen. Everyone likes football and the national team and follows their star players. The Yemeni people are the same as anyone else.”

Most of the players are based at home and before the 27th edition of the Gulf Cup, Yemen was the only one of the eight never to have won the tournament and have never got out of the group.

It is hard for the players to keep fully focused on football while in Saudi Arabia. “They worry about what is going on in the country and they hope their families are OK,” the coach said. “This is normal, but they are professional and I ask them to try to focus on the games. I have lived this situation before, I have geopolitics experience in the region.”

Ould Ali spent three years in charge of Palestine from 2018 to 2021, after more than four years as an assistant coach. Instability is not an unfamiliar theme for him. “Each situation is different. Yemen is a problem between Yemenis, not between outside countries.

skip past newsletter promotion Free newsletter | Fortnightly Sign up to The Hotspot A new fortnightly newsletter covering the intersection of sport and the climate crisis Enter your email Sign up after newsletter promotion

View image in fullscreen Algeria’s Noureddine Ould Ali is used to instability. He coached Palestine before his stint with Yemen. Photograph: ZUMA Press Inc/Alamy Live News

“For a coach, Palestine was very difficult. The Israeli soldiers used to stop me for eight to 10 hours before I could go to work. The players are not free and when we played overseas they stopped the players. It was a pleasure for me to work with Palestine, their difficulties are not made by Palestinians.”

A reunion with Palestine is not impossible at the 2027 Asian Cup, which will also be hosted in Saudi Arabia. In June, Yemen, slightly surprisingly, defeated Lebanon to become the last team to qualify for the quadrennial tournament. “It was a great day for Yemen football and we hope we could make people back home smile for a while.”

In January, Yemen return to Jeddah for their opening game against South Korea and players such as Atlético Madrid’s Lee Kang-in, Kim Min-jae of Bayern Munich and Son Heung-min. It will be a step up from the Gulf Cup and the people back home will be watching.

“Again, we will try to make the people at home proud,” says Ould Ali. “It would be very nice to give the world a different headline about Yemen. When we are united we feel we can beat anyone.”

Sports.title: Revealed: Cristiano Ronaldo could be slapped with a six-month BAN after walking out on Portugal - as the country's prime minister reveals talks with the 'betrayed' 41-year-old star
Sports.content:
Revealed: Cristiano Ronaldo could be slapped with a six-month BAN after walking out on Portugal - as the country's prime minister reveals talks with the 'betrayed' 41-year-old star

Cristiano Ronaldo could be facing a ban of up to six months from the Portugal national team after sensationally storming out of the team's training camp amid a row with manager Jorge Jesus.

The star, 41, landed in Madrid in the early hours of Thursday morning after flying from Copenhagen, where Portugal are due to face Denmark, on his private jet.

He had been seen leaving the Parken Stadium in the Danish capital on Wednesday after missing a third consecutive training session.

Ronaldo later confirmed in a statement on Instagram that he had left the team's camp because of comments made by Jesus in his press conference.

The Portugal boss said the captain would not start the Denmark clash, just days after sitting on the bench for the entirety of the 2-1 win in Norway, but insisted there was no issue between the two.

And reports in Portugal claim Ronaldo could be suspended from playing for his country for between one and six months if he is found to have 'abandoned' the team.

Cristiano Ronaldo (left) sensationally walked out on Portugal amid a dispute with his manager

The Portuguese Football Federation's disciplinary code states: 'Any player who, having been regularly called up, unjustifiably abandons or fails to appear for training, a match, or any activity of the national teams or related to the sporting representation of the FPF or Portugal, will be sanctioned with a suspension of one to six months.'

Ronaldo said: 'After the national team coach's press conference, and following a conversation with the President of the Portuguese Football Federation, I have decided to leave the national team training camp.

'In due time, I will tell all Portuguese people the truth about the reasons that led to my departure from the national team, to which I have always dedicated myself.

'Now is the time to wish good luck to Portugal and to all my teammates.'

Ronaldo's decision to quit the Portuguese camp has sparked suggestions he may retire from international duty and has even prompted the intervention of the country's Prime Minister, Luís Montenegro.

Record reports Montenegro has discussed the issue with Ronaldo, as well as Jesus and Pedro Proenca, the head of the Portuguese FA.

It is unclear whether Montenegro was attempting to resolve a dispute described as an 'earthquake' in Portugal, or if he was merely wanting to be briefed.

Speaking before the Denmark game, Jesus insisted he had a 'completely' clear conscience amid the Ronaldo saga. 'It was a frantic few hours because we had two games,' he added.

'Now we have another one... Besides, I've been in football for many years and I know I didn't do anything to prevent the situation from continuing as before.'

Footage published by A Bola showed Jesus and Proenca being booed by a small group of fans who had gathered outside the team's hotel in Copenhagen before the team made the short journey to Parken Stadium.

Reports in Portugal claim the dispute in the national team camp has reached Prime Minister Luis Montenegro

Ronaldo's sister Elma has come out in support of her brother after his shock exit from the Portugal camp (Source: Elma_Official/Instagram)

Ronaldo's sister, Elma Aveiro, had earlier fanned the flames of controversy by claiming Portuguese people 'deserve mediocrity' because of their treatment of the country's record goalscorer.

'The national team deserved better structuring,' she wrote on Instagram. 'The Portuguese press deserved more competence and fewer guesses.

'As for the Portuguese... well, they don't deserve the best in anything. We are envious, contemptuous, ignorant, and we deserve to return to the mediocrity we always had in football before CR7. Thank you for everything CR7!'

Elma was not the only supporter from inside Ronaldo's camp to suggest that the five-time Ballon d'Or winner had been treated unfairly, with Spanish journalist Edu Aguirre - who is friends with the Al-Nassr superstar - claiming he had been 'betrayed' by Jesus.

'There was a meeting yesterday, Tuesday night,' he told Spanish programme El Chiringuito. 'A meeting between the Federation president, the coach, and Cristiano. Jorge Jesus apologized to Cristiano for the disregard shown in making him warm up for 30 minutes instead of playing him.

'And not only did he apologize privately, but he also told him he would apologize publicly, that he would publicly admit his mistake. That's Jorge Jesus's promise to Cristiano. And then he goes to the press conference and tells this many lies that nobody believes.

'That's why Cristiano explodes, because he feels betrayed. There's nothing more to it, it's really like that. Your coach comes to you privately: "Look, see, this is how it was, you understand me, okay, I didn't manage the situation well, we're in this together, I'm sorry. If there's a press conference, I'll clarify everything, I'll apologize, don't worry, everything will be fine, everything will be resolved." Then you go to the press conference 12 hours later and leave Cristiano still...

'Worse, you're acting tough, saying that you're the one in charge and that Cristiano is just another player. Go home and move on. That's why I say: betrayal.'

Ronaldo confirmed on Wednesday night that he had left the camp amid a row with Jorge Jesus

The captain confirmed he had withdrawn from the squad because of Jesus's comments

Ronaldo held talks with Jesus and Proenca on Wednesday morning, a meeting initially described as amicable.

But the rift between Ronaldo and his manager appeared to deepen after Jesus's press conference.

Jesus admitted Ronaldo had been 'angry' with him, with footage showing the captain walking off down the tunnel after sitting out the victory in Norway.

Jesus, who also worked with Ronaldo at Al-Nassr, said: 'There was no incident whatsoever.

'Any player - and I was a player myself - when you spend 20 or 30 minutes warming up and then don't get on, no-one is happy about that.

'Afterwards, as coach, I decided not to bring him on. It's nothing to make a fuss about.'

Jesus also suggested Goncalo Ramos would keep his place in the side ahead of Ronaldo for the Denmark match. 'If I need [Ronaldo], he'll come on,' he said. 'If I don't need him, he won't.'

Jesus had originally planned to bring on the veteran striker for a 30-minute cameo but then decided to leave him on the bench, which has seemingly sparked the feud.

It is an inauspicious start to the relationship between Jesus and Ronaldo, who opted not to retire from international duty after the World Cup.

Only a week ago, Ronaldo reiterated his commitment to the cause, saying: 'I had a conversation with our president, with our coach (about his future).

'I still believe that I'm able to help the national team to reach what they want, and will finish when I feel like I'm not doing anything here.

'I think I can give to the national team my support, not only through the goals, but also outside of football.

'This is a new young generation. But for me the basic point is to be able on the pitch to score the goals and to help the team win games.'

Ronaldo will turn 42 in February and has scored three goals in five games for Al-Nassr so far in the Saudi Pro League this season.

Sports.title: THE AUDIT - Manchester United: Michael Carrick under pressure, simmering fan fury and summer recruitment starting to bite - but gold mine academy still in rude health despite JJ Gabriel bombshell
Sports.content:
THE AUDIT - Manchester United: Michael Carrick under pressure, simmering fan fury and summer recruitment starting to bite - but gold mine academy still in rude health despite JJ Gabriel bombshell

THE AUDIT is a new series from Daily Mail Sport assessing the true health of Premier League clubs in the short, medium and long term. Here, we go beneath the surface at Manchester United to review the state of play on and off the pitch at Old Trafford.

No one at Manchester United is kidding themselves it has been a positive start to the season. At least, not anymore. One win in five Premier League games and a painful Carabao Cup exit to Brighton has punctured the mood of optimism building under Michael Carrick.

‘It’s not that bad,’ Carrick argued after Ainsley Maitland-Niles’s stunning late equaliser denied United victory at Everton at the start of September. ‘There are moments we can deal with a bit better, but we’ll be fine.’

Ten days later, after United had lost the Manchester derby and Brighton became the first team in 50 years to overturn a two-goal deficit to win at Old Trafford, Carrick struck a very different tone.

‘We can't accept that as a group,’ he admitted. ‘It feels bad at the moment because we haven't had a great two or three weeks. We've got to win football matches and obviously we've got to do it pretty quickly.’

It has been a challenging season so far on the pitch, and United have suffered off it too. Fan unrest and protests over the club’s clampdown on ticket touting, teen star JJ Gabriel’s bombshell decision to quit and news that the cost of servicing United’s debt since the Glazer takeover in 2005 has now topped £1billion has added to the early-season gloom.

So what's the state of play, and how healthy is the club behind the scenes?

It's been a turbulent start to the season for Manchester United, with poor results on the pitch and bad news off it

FIRST-TEAM SQUAD: 5/10

United appeared to be in good shape after Carrick returned to the club in January as Ruben Amorim’s replacement and led the team to a third-place finish in May.

Armed with an extra £100million from Champions League qualification, United looked ready to compete with their rivals for top players this summer as they embarked on a midfield rebuild.

Elliot Anderson was widely touted as United’s No1 target. Aurelien Tchouameni and Sandro Tonali were among the other big names mentioned. In the end, Anderson went to Manchester City for £116m and Tottenham got Tonali for £100m. Tchouameni stayed at Real Madrid.

It felt like United were never really shopping at the same level. They spent £163m, less than Hull City and roughly the same as Ipswich Town.

United were beaten to West Ham’s £85m midfielder Mateus Fernandes by Spurs and pulled the plug on a £38.5m deal for Ederson of Atalanta, before signing Carlos Baleba (£70m), Andrey Santos (£50m) and Youri Tielemans (£35m) – plus back-up goalkeeper Karl Darlow as a free agent and academy signing Tynan Thompson (£8m) from Tottenham.

Baleba has yet to kick a ball for the club after making the matchday squad for the first time at Fulham in the last game before the international break. Santos was dropped after a disastrous opening-day defeat at Hull and has only made one other start, in the loss to Brighton.

United’s recruitment policy has come under fire for focusing on the midfield and ignoring the need for another striker or cover at left back for Luke Shaw. Having missed the entire pre-season with a persistent shin injury, Benjamin Sesko made just two starts before suffering a relapse, leaving Carrick without a conventional striker.

An injury to Amad Diallo has prevented Bryan Mbeumo from switching from the right flank to replace Sesko through the middle, as he did during the summer friendlies. Matheus Cunha has had to play as a false nine, and a very false one at that.

One of United's key summer signings Andrey Santos, who cost £50m from Chelsea, was dropped after a disastrous opening-day defeat at Hull, and has only made one other start

Having missed pre-season with a persistent shin injury, Benjamin Sesko made just two starts before suffering a relapse, leaving United without a conventional striker

Shaw lasted just three games before his unbroken run of 41 league appearances came to an end, forcing Carrick to try Patrick Dorgu and Noussair Mazraoui at left back.

A reluctance not to overspend on new signings might make sense on the balance sheet, but United have looked decidedly average so far. Five points is their worst return from the opening five games of a Premier League season and they are already out of one domestic cup.

Worryingly, the fixture list has been quite kind to United, and the reality of juggling Premier League and Champions League commitments hasn’t started to bite yet.

After the international break, Tottenham visit Old Trafford before a run of three away games at Atletico Madrid, high-flying Leeds United and Como, before playing Bournemouth at home and Chelsea away to round out October.

MANAGERIAL STAFF: 5/10

Carrick has been around United long enough as a player and coach to know how this works: succeed like he did in the second half of last season, and he is the man with the red of United in his blood who can bring back the glory days.

Fail like he has at the start of this season, and he is Ole Gunnar Solskjaer Mk II – the homespun hero who makes a compelling argument to land the job on a full-time basis and never quite hits the same heights again.

We’re only seven games into the new season, but even a coach with Carrick’s experience of the Old Trafford circus seems shocked at how quickly the tide has turned against him and his team.

The fans rounded on them after the Brighton defeat, and there were more boos when he substituted Kobbie Mainoo in the draw at Fulham before the international break.

Carrick must use these three weeks as a chance to reset and regroup with his coaching staff. The 45-year-old has branded early-season speculation over his future as ‘ridiculous’, but he simply cannot allow results to continue like this.

Yes, United can count themselves a little unlucky with Maitland-Niles’ equaliser for Everton, and the decision to allow Erling Haaland’s goal in the derby. But they got the breaks in their only Premier League win over Ipswich, and a fortunate deflection late on to claim a point at Fulham. It’s not as though United fans are cursing their luck.

We’re only seven games into the new season, but even a coach with Carrick’s experience of the Old Trafford circus seems shocked at how quickly the tide has turned against him

Carrick’s former team-mate Gary Neville lambasted the performance at Craven Cottage as ‘an absolute disgrace’ – specifically United’s reluctance to run, which was borne out by the stats.

There is a perception that the team’s passive nature mirrors that of the head coach, and Carrick has had to defend the lack of passion – both his own and the team’s – on several occasions.

His No2 Steve Holland and assistants Jonathan Woodgate, Jonny Evans and Travis Binnion were praised for their contributions in the second half of last season, and this backroom team that was rather hastily put together brought their individual strengths to the table.

Carrick will need their support again in the weeks ahead as he tries to overcome the early problems and inject some positivity into the club.

ACADEMY SET-UP: 6/10

The youth academy is a source of huge pride at United, so it has been particularly painful to see Gabriel turn his back on the club and ask for his registration to be ripped up.

Who knows what his reasons are. Sources close to the 15-year-old phenomenon say his family believe there are better clubs than United to give Gabriel the platform to make the most of his talent.

There have been gripes over his pathway into the first team since the summer – even though his demand to go came on the eve of a potential senior debut in the Carabao Cup against Brighton.

More cynical observers would focus on the timing, just a few weeks short of his 16th birthday when he can appoint an agent and use his Irish passport to join a foreign club. There was little surprise when it emerged that his camp have held talks with Real Madrid and Barcelona.

While losing Gabriel would be a huge blow to United, there is no shortage of talent knocking on the first-team door or coming through the pipeline.

Shea Lacey showed why Carrick gave him plenty of game time in pre-season by scoring on his full debut against Brighton

But 15-year-old wonderkid JJ Gabriel dropped a bombshell on United by asking to have his registration ripped up

Shea Lacey showed why Carrick gave him plenty of game time in pre-season by scoring on his full debut against Brighton. The 19-year-old winger was predicted to be one of the young players making an impact on the senior squad this season along with the Fletcher twins, Tyler and Jack.

Jim Thwaites and Noah Ajayi, who has just signed his first professional contract, aren’t far behind. Thompson is another to watch out for after United agreed a deal with Tottenham worth up to £8m to sign the 18-year-old winger in the summer.

The club are continuing to recruit at academy level as they invest in the future, and have signed three promising youngsters in Karim Cassim, David Eze and Isaac Konde during the international break.

BOARDROOM/OWNERS: 2/10

It hasn’t taken long for festering anger with United’s owners to erupt into open hostility early in the new season.

Fans have harboured an intense dislike of the Glazer family for some time. The club’s full-year results last week revealed that the cost of financing United’s debt has now topped the £1bn mark for the first time since the Americans’ leveraged takeover in 2005.

Increasingly, though, their fury is being directed towards Sir Jim Ratcliffe and Ineos who have assumed day-to-day running of the club since the billionaire’s minority takeover nearly three years ago.

They are unhappy at Ratcliffe’s treatment of season-ticket holders, and that has reached a new low in the wake of a controversial crackdown on ticket touting that they claim has targeted innocent supporters.

There was a demonstration organised by protest group The 1958 before the Manchester derby when The Red Army also left the Stretford End empty of all flags and banners except one that declared: ‘The way you treat us is a disgrace.’

Ratcliffe hasn’t helped by doubling down on his criticism of the UK’s immigration system, prompting the Manchester United Muslim Supporters Club to issue a vote of no confidence in the owners.

United fans protested about the club's owners and skyrocketing season ticket prices earlier this month

There was a demonstration organised by protest group The 1958 before the Manchester derby when The Red Army also left the Stretford End empty of all flags and banners except this one

FINANCES: 4/10

Ratcliffe issued a stark warning last year that United could have gone bust by Christmas were it not for the cost-cutting and redundancies carried out by Ineos, and the latest financial results demonstrated that United’s problems won’t be solved overnight.

The club’s total debt still stands at £1.15bn, made up of £577.6m from the Glazer takeover in 2005, £200m owing on the club’s revolving credit facility and outstanding transfer fees of £375m.

Worse still, the £69.6m paid in interest – an increase of £48.4m (228.3 per cent) from the previous year – pushed the cost of financing that debt over the last 21 years past the £1bn mark.

Despite record revenues of £677.6m and turning an £18.4m operating loss into a £22.6m profit over the last year, United still reported an overall net loss of £43m.

Being back in the Champions League will help, but it’s a measure of the club’s desperation to claw back money wherever possible that miniature cubes of the Old Trafford pitch that was ripped up over the summer are on sale for £125.

United will point to the balance sheet as a reason why they couldn’t overspend on new signings in the summer. They have also been trying to drive down the wage bill by offloading big earners like Casemiro and Jadon Sancho, and offering more incentivised contracts.

But they couldn’t find a taker for Marcus Rashford, largely because of his £325,000-a-week salary, and now face tricky negotiations with captain Bruno Fernandes who knows he can earn substantially more elsewhere.

Saving money on transfer fees and wages is one thing. But if it means that you can’t compete for the top targets and there is a danger your best players leave, it’s a false economy.

STADIUM: 5/10

Despite the financial worries, United remain committed to building a new £2bn stadium to replace Old Trafford funded by private investment.

The club have paid £63.5m to purchase a 25-acre triangle of land located 350 metres away from Old Trafford, and will shortly begin a consultation process with fans over the design of the new 100,000-seater venue. It’s hoped that it can be completed in time to host the 2035 Women’s World Cup final.

In the meantime, United continue to patch up Old Trafford. The pitch has been re-laid for the first time in 14 years, including new foundations and drainage system. However, there is only so much that can be done to fix the roof which sprung another leak when the first home game of the season against Ipswich was hit by a deluge of rain.

The club also received a number of complaints over the standards in hospitality suites after making changes over the summer, while local residents have challenged plans to open a new 1,300-capacity fan zone behind the Stretford End next month.

For all its faults, however, Old Trafford is still one of the most iconic venues in British sport. It holds a special place in the hearts of many supporters who are waiting to find out what the new stadium will look like and how much importance will be placed on rank-and-file fans.

Sports.title: Disgraced Team USA gymnastics doctor Larry Nassar is quietly REMOVED from Michigan sex offender registry
Sports.content:
Disgraced Team USA gymnastics doctor Larry Nassar has been quietly removed from the Michigan Sex Offender Registry list.

Nassar, who served as team doctor for the national gymnastics team from 1996 to 2014, used his position to exploit hundreds of young athletes, including medal-winning Olympic gymnasts Simone Biles and Aly Raisman.

He is currently serving multiple prison sentences lasting decades after being convicted on multiple counts of sexual abuse and child pornography in both federal and state court.

According to the Eaton County (Michigan) Prosecutor's Office, the 63-year-old is among more than 20,000 people whose names have been removed from the sex offender list after the Michigan State Police recently purged thousands of individuals from the database whose crimes happened before July 1, 2011.

A Michigan Supreme Court ruling on September 9 said that amendments to the Sex offender Registration Act issued in 2021 cannot be used to retroactively require registration due to older incidents, leading to the purge of the database.

The prosecutor's office wrote on social media that: 'The Michigan Supreme Court's decision to eliminate SORA requirements for these offenders is deeply concerning. Our community, along with the victims of these crimes, expected the registry to provide a measure of protection and awareness—assurances that have now been removed by the Court's ruling.'

Larry Nasser has been quietly removed from the Michigan Sex Offenders Registry List

Nasser is serving decades in prison after being convicted of multiple crimes

The registry is intended to 'assist the public' with preventing future criminal sexual acts by convicted sex offenders, according to Michigan State Police, and typically lists a legal name, photo, primary address, work address, age, physical description and court with records relevant to the criminal conviction.

'His conduct occurred before 2011 despite his convictions coming after,' said The Eaton County Prosecutor's Office, confirming Nasser's removal, per CBS News.

The prosecutor's office claimed the Supreme Court could have applied for a different interpretation and allowed for certain sex offenders to stay on the list.

More than 150 gymnasts were abused by Nassar during his 30-year career. Nassar admitted to sexually assaulting the athletes when he worked at Michigan State University and USA Gymnastics.

The doctor also admitted to possessing child pornography, and more than 100 women sought over $1billion from the federal government for the FBI's failure to stop him.

He was sentenced in federal court in 2017 to 60 years in prison on charges of possessing child sex abuse material. The following year, Nassar was sentenced to up to 175 years and up to 125 years, respectively, in two separate Michigan courts for molesting female gymnasts under his care.

Following the federal sentencing, U.S. Attorney Birge said: 'Today was a day of reckoning for Larry Nassar. He more than deserves this punishment for what he did.

'He consumed child pornography on a massive scale. We found 37,000 images of child pornography on his computers. Insatiable hunger of that nature simply encourages those who produce such images to continue to sexually exploit children. Compounding his danger to the public,

'Nassar was an insidious hands-on child predator in his own right. He took advantage of family friendships. And he treated his license to practice medicine as a license to sexually molest children. Thanks to the brave victims who came forward, we learned the full scope of his depravity. The breadth and dark depth of his heinous acts are extraordinary.'

Larry Nassar is pictured in court during his sentencing hearing in Michigan in January 2018

Olympic icon Simone Biles was among Nasser's long list of hundreds of victims

In April 2024, the US Justice Department announced a $138.7 million settlement with more than 100 people who accused the FBI of grossly mishandling allegations of sexual assault against Nassar in 2015 and 2016, a critical time gap that allowed the sports doctor to continue to prey on victims before his arrest.

When combined with other settlements, $1billion now has been set aside by various organizations to compensate hundreds of women who said Nassar assaulted them under the guise of treatment for sports injuries.

Simone Biles publicly broke her silence in January 2018, revealing in a powerful tweet that she was one of Nassar's victims.

'It took me a long time to write that, probably a couple of days, because every time I would go to write, I would start balling, and I couldn't get through it,' she said.

Biles also noted that she was heartbroken over having to continue to train at the ranch, the former USA Gymnastics national training center where she and her teammates were abused by the disgraced doctor.

Sports.title: Bungling Andy Burnham is criticised for ANOTHER error in attempting to clarify his statement on Man City case after being called out for 'tone-deaf' response following 'concern' over losing Abu Dhabi owners
Sports.content:
Prime Minister Andy Burnham has received further backlash after Number 10 attempted to clarify his comments around the financial case surrounding Manchester City. Burnham's claim that he would be 'really concerned' if Manchester City's owners were to sell the club after it was found guilty of serious breaches of the Premier League's financial regulations has been hit by widespread criticism. The Prime Minister made the comments following confirmation from the league that Man City had been found to have created a slew of 'sham' deals and contracts which misled the Premier League over £900million-plus in sponsorship deals over a nine-year period. 'As the Prime Minister made clear, the initial judgement is serious and there can't be any suggestion that anyone is above the rules,' a spokesperson said on Thursday. 'He also stressed that it is an ongoing independent process. It is essential that it is allowed to run its course and the outcome respected. 'If wrongdoing is established, those responsible should face the appropriate consequences.' Football fans, though, haven't taken kindly to the latest message. 'Wrongdoing has already been established,' one fan posted on X. 'Get them gone.' Another shared: 'This is an equally bad statement. Wrongdoing has already been established.' A third posted: 'Burnham is a joke. We all heard what he said. He's backtracking, not clarifying.' Andy Burnham (with Man City chairman Khaldoon Al-Mubarak in 2019) has been criticised for comments made on his 'concern' that the club's ownership might sell

Your browser does not support iframes.

The Premier League's chief executive Richard Masters stated that the club had 'systematically broken' the rules for nearly a decade and called the decision by the Independent Commission who heard the case 'the most significant in Premier League history'. Since confirmation of the decision broke on Tuesday evening, there have been calls for Man City to face relegation, fines, and even expulsion from the top flight, as well as arguments that the Abu Dhabi ownership group should move on – but former mayor of Greater Manchester Burnham took a more hesitant tone and lingered on the investment they had made into both the club and the city. Those on social media were quick to suggest that Burnham's comments could likely interfere with the process of both Man City's appeal and potential future sanctions if the charges are upheld. One fan posted: 'It was a confusing and, at best, tone-deaf intervention. Coming from a skilled operator, it was quite jarring.' Stan Collymore suggested that Burnham's 'concern' was 'tone deaf', highlighting the 'clunky' comments as an example of the power of sports-washing. 'For a PM, the day after a judgement by a respected panel to say 'we can't afford to lose City Group, they've put a lot into Manchester' is missing the point so widely that he's now going to be tagged as taking a side or grossly naïve,' he wrote in a lengthy post on X. 'Neither things people will readily vote for.' Rio Ferdinand added that he thought Burnham was 'on the back foot referencing Manchester City', but other commenters on the site were more critical. 'This is political interference,' one wrote. 'Already stating that he sees them as a positive influence and not wanting them gone. Unacceptable interference by influencing the (government's Football) Regulator.' Another added: 'Absolutely disgusting statement from the PM. He's basically saying you can cheat the system all you want if you pay enough. Just shows what sort of morals he really has'. Green Party deputy leader Mothin Ali also weighed in, saying: 'Andy Burnham's comments are staggering, just one day after saying people should come before profit, he sides with big money over the integrity of a sport that belongs to the people. 'It's a shame the prime minister appears to agree there should be one rule for the rich and one for everyone else.' Conservative MP Louie French, who serves as shadow minister for Digital, Culture, Media and Sport warned: 'Burnham's clumsy comments haven't just undermined the ongoing legal process and Premier League. He's left the IFR Chief, who is a Labour donor and will determine the fit and proper owner test, exposed to future legal challenges, as we warned would happen.' Burnham has received backlash for his comments as a statement trying to clarify what he said was released Burnham's comments did attract praise from one corner of social media, with Man City supporter and Oasis frontman Liam Gallagher writing: 'There's only 1 ANDY BURNHAM.' Burnham, whose mayoral tenure in Greater Manchester began three years after the 2014 deal struck between Manchester Council and the Abu Dhabi United Group worth £1billion promising a regeneration of city centre districts New Islington and Ancoats, had stressed in his remarks that he was unable to 'intervene' in the ongoing case. Speaking at the home of his side Everton at the Hill Dickinson Stadium, he said: 'I would be really concerned to lose (Man City's Abu Dhabi owners). 'They've been such a huge partner in the building of modern Manchester and obviously the building of Manchester City into the global force that it is. 'I can't intervene more in the process. It would be wrong for me to do that. It would be wrong, I think, to jump to a conclusion before having really studied all of the detail, but obviously it's ongoing, and because it's still contested by Manchester City, then I think it's right that I don't say much more.' 'I do actually thank the City Football Group and the wider ownership for the money that they didn't just put into the Etihad (Stadium) and the campus around it but also into the city.' In 2023, when charges were first brought against Man City, Abu Dhabi warned the United Kingdom that a negative outcome might damage relations with the country. Man City have until October 2 to appeal the verdict, and Evertonian Burnham added that he did not want to assume guilt, as some had done in the wake of the Toffees' own sanctions in 2023. 'Everton was in this position a few years ago and you might remember that I fought for Everton in that situation because I still hold the view very firmly that they weren't fairly treated in that process,' he continued. 'I remember people proclaiming Everton guilty at the time and with hindsight I think more people would say that wasn't fair, the way that was handled. 'So it would be wrong of me to leap to one side given the experience that I'd had before becoming prime minister.' Everton had fallen foul of the Premier League's financial regulations and were charged and deducted ten points, later reduced to six on appeal. But this was the scenario Man City seem to have been looking to avoid during the 2009-18 period scrutinised by the Independent Commission. David Kogan, chairman of the Independent Football Regulator (IFR), stated that he had the powers to 'assess the suitability of owners, directors and executive' and that the body would look to use their powers to protect 'the sustainability, honesty and integrity of English football'. The IFR and the FA will assess the findings once the sanctioning and appeals process has been completed. Man City continue to deny any wrongdoing, with chief executive Ferran Soriano stating in a video shared with the club's staff that they were in possession of 'irrefutable evidence' of their innocence that could dispel the Premier League's 'conspiracy theory' on appeal.
