By diversifying Canada's exports away from the U.S., officials said Canada will be able to charge a higher price for the oil it currently ships south of the border, providing what could be an additional $10 billion a year in revenues.

The federal government also said that once approved, the project will create up to 140,000 jobs.

Dominic LeBlanc, the minister of one Canadian economy, has been tasked with completing the conditions document setting out the requirements for the project by Sept. 1, 2027, allowing construction to begin, with a view to having the pipeline up and running by 2032-33.

Carney said the work of crafting those conditions will be supported by the Major Projects Office and the Canada Energy Regulator who will hold consultations with stakeholders to determine environmental protections, oversight, Indigenous ownership and local hiring.

The estimated cost of the project is between $35.2 billion and $43.7 billion, which includes a contingency.

The Alberta government and the federally owned Trans Mountain Corporation would each own 45 per cent of the pipeline, with the Calgary-based Pembina Pipeline Corporation owning a 10 per cent stake through the construction phase.

Once the pipeline is up and running, the Pembina Pipeline Corporation will have the opportunity to purchase an additional 10 per cent stake.

Carney said that Indigenous communities will be offered a minimum 10 per cent ownership stake in the project.

Increasing private sector ownership

While the pipeline is 90 per cent owned by the federal and Alberta governments, a senior official speaking on background explained that there are investors poised to take part.

The official said that those investors are currently watching to see if Canada is capable of fast-tracking the approval and construction of the Pacific Link by 2032-33.

Workers lay pipe during construction of the Trans Mountain pipeline expansion on farmland, in Abbotsford, B.C., in 2023. A new West Coast pipeline will ship one million barrels of oil a day from Alberta to the B.C. coast once it opens in 2032-33. (Darryl Dyck/The Canadian Press)

Those investors are cautious, the official explained, because of how fraught the approval process was for the Trans Mountain Pipeline and how long it took to build.

Carney said Thursday's announcement — where Alberta, B.C. and Indigenous communities are all involved in the project — and that Canada's effective tax rate for investments has been cut to less than a third of the G7 average are reasons private investors will be attracted to the project.

"This is the best country in the world, major economy in the world, to invest. And I'm sure those companies and companies across the country will take that into account," he said.

Higher emissions, lower intensity

Thursday's announcement was welcomed by business groups such as the Canadian Chamber of Commerce which commended the Liberal government for providing up-front regulatory backing for the project.

"Getting our resources to Asia-Pacific markets is a path to more production, prosperity and a brighter future for workers, their families and communities," said the chamber's Bryan Detchou in a statement.

Environmental organizations like Greenpeace and the Pembina Institute, however, said Canada shouldn't be pulling more oil out of the ground.

"New oilsands and pipeline projects will drive emissions even higher," the Pembina Institute, which is not affiliated with the pipeline corporation, said in a post on X.

"Every fraction of a degree matters. Canada should be investing in cleaner, more resilient energy solutions."

WATCH | Carney says Pacific Link pipeline demonstrates 'power of Canada': Ahead of Alberta referendum, Pacific Link pipeline demonstrates 'power of Canada': Carney | Duration closed caption 2:51 Prime Minister Mark Carney said designating the Pacific Link pipeline in the national interest shows 'Canada is working,' when asked what message Albertans supporting a separation referendum should take from the announcement.

A government explanatory note says that while the pipeline "does not directly contribute to Canada's greenhouse gas emission reduction targets," it is a key part of plans to reduce emissions intensity, or emissions per barrel of oil produced.

That plan includes the Pathways Project, a carbon capture and storage initiative that Carney said will absorb as much as 16 million tonnes of carbon emissions annually and store them underground.

Carney said that the Pathways Project is only part of his government's environmental mitigation plans which also include $1.2 billion in federal funding for ocean protections announced on Tuesday.

Carney said choosing a southern route, instead of a route through northern British Columbia, will ensure the project does not cross "highly sensitive ecosystems, including the Great Bear Sea."

The 1,200-kilometre pipeline will carry bitumen through southern Alberta from Bruderheim to a deepwater port near Delta, B.C, where infrastructure at the Roberts Bank terminal will be expanded.

Carney said his government's new oceans funding will include "a series of measures to protect the habitats of killer whales" during the expansion of Roberts Bank.

The federal government's explanatory note says an agreement in principle with Alberta to reduce methane emissions by 75 per below 2014 levels by 2035 is a key component of "Canada's plan to strengthen its position in global energy markets, as customers across the world prioritize low-carbon oil and gas."

NDP and Conservatives weigh in

NDP Leader Avi Lewis accused the Liberal government of rushing the project through the approvals process "while sweeping aside environmental protections."

"It is an offence to Canadian science, public health, collective safety and common sense. And it is a gift to an oil industry already on track to make $100 billion in wartime profits this year alone," he said.

"This project leaves Canadians bearing all the risks of a bad investment without any of the rewards."

Just Asking wants to know: What questions do you have about Prime Minister Mark Carney's plan to fast-track major projects and how that plan would affect environmental protection? Send us your questions before our Oct. 3 show.

Conservative Leader Pierre Poilievre said his party strongly supports a pipeline and congratulated Alberta Premier Danielle Smith for championing the project.

"It has taken Mark Carney almost a year and a half to put one proposal on a national interest list. We need a pipeline in the ground, not just on a list," he said.

"The federal government needs to get out of the way and let builders build, investors invest and workers work."

World.title: Canada Malting plant could collapse at any moment, engineering report says
World.content:
The audio version of this article is generated by AI-based technology. Mispronunciations can occur. We are working with our partners to continually review and improve the results.

The Canada Malting plant, which looms over Montreal’s Sud-Ouest borough and is notably home to the mysterious “pink house,” could collapse at any moment, according to a new engineering report.

The report says the structure — a mass of brick and concrete silos towering over the Lachine Canal to its south and St-Ambroise Street to its north — represents an “imminent danger” to public safety.

“Controlled demolition is the only possible, safe and rational solution to eliminate the critical danger that this building represents,” wrote the report’s author, André Houle from the engineering firm STP ING inc.

Houle is especially concerned about a facade wall, which he says has detached from the roof and is “hanging by a thread.” He’s worried about this brick facade falling onto St-Ambroise Street, where people walk and cars are currently parked.

“The only way to protect the public with this project right now is to close the street, there’s no other way,” Houle said in an interview with CBC.

Images from an engineering report show the state of the inside of the Canada Malting plant on the banks of the Lachine Canal. (STP ING inc.)

The danger of collapse could worsen in the winter or spring, his report says. Freeze-thaw cycles could contribute to the collapse, as could vibrations from an earthquake.

Private developer ready to build

The engineering report is the latest development weighing in on the future of the structure, which has lain vacant since 1985.

In a media release, La Malterie inc., a subsidiary of Renwick, the company that owns and plans to develop the site, said a demolition request had been submitted to the city.

Part of St-Ambroise Street will be closed in the meantime.

The city said in a statement on Thursday that it was analyzing the demolition request to "ensure that the emergency demolition of part of the site is justified."

Antoine Poulin, the chief of staff for Véronique Fournier, the mayor of the Sud-Ouest borough, said in an interview that the city met with the developer and with Houle earlier this week.

He said the city had to conduct its own review of the site before greenlighting a demolition request, particularly given the important heritage of the Canada Malting plant.

He emphasized that the main area of concern in Houle's report is the crumbling brick facade off St-Ambroise Street, and that the report does not say that the other sides of the building, which are adjacent to a bar and recreational path, are in as dire condition.

The Malting factory is a collection of buildings, erected in 1905, that the À nous la Malting collective says is big enough for 200 social housing units. (Jonathan Montpetit/CBC)

Noam Schnitzer, the president of Renwick, said in a statement that the former Canada Malting site holds a "unique place in the history of Saint-Henri and in Montreal's industrial legacy.

“We remain fully committed to ensuring that the identity of this iconic site can live on through the future La Malterie project.”

La Malterie Inc. said its plan for the site includes 685 housing units, 20 per cent of which would be social housing. The plan also includes community spaces, businesses and community services. The company says it will also preserve the “pink house.”

The developer, the city and the community group À nous la Malting have clashed over the future of the site for years .

The group wants to turn the building into a collectively owned complex with 200 affordable rental units, a rooftop garden, a bike repair shop, a public daycare, a community kitchen and a museum.

Members of the group camped outside the plant in 2023 to protest Renwick’s development plan. They had pushed for the site to be used exclusively for social housing.

The Malting plant and elevators were built in 1905 by the Canada Malting Co. Large and cement silos were added in the 1940s to store barley.

The company exported the malt along the Lachine Canal, and when the canal closed to commercial navigation in 1970, the transportation cost rose to the point that the company abandoned the site in the 1980s.

Since then, it has fallen into disrepair. Windows are boarded up, brick walls are crumbling, and the facade is covered in graffiti.

And, though Renwick has set up barriers to prevent people from entering the building, it is popular with “ urban explorers ” and is home to the “pink house” — a small shack, painted pink and well maintained, which sits atop the crumbling plant.

Engineer says street should have closed earlier

Houle says he’s amazed people are still going into the building, given how dangerous it is. He described arches, made of bricks and steel, that have become especially hazardous.

“When that structure is rusted, it doesn’t hold the brick anymore and the brick falls on the ground,” he explained. “Left and right, the bricks are falling on the ground.”

The STP ING inc. report released Thursday warns that anyone entering the building risks death. In images, the report shows falling bricks and floors that are worn through.

Houle believes the area should’ve been closed one week ago.

“Anywhere else it would be, ‘we’ll close off the street and we’ll do the paperwork after. Because the safety is an issue,’” he said. “Here, we’re saying to the owner, ‘no… you need to go through the approval process.’”

“When it’s an urgent matter, there’s a safety issue, why do you have to wait for the paperwork to be able to act?”

Poulin, the city spokesperson, said the city had to follow a simple procedure to approve the street closure, and he said the developer, and Houle, were aware of it.

Fournier, the borough mayor, said in a statement that it's the developer's responsibility to secure the street. She added that the developer is also responsible for communicating with residents of the area.

Fournier said any development that happens on the site will have to meet clear conditions that have been set for it. That includes having a high proportion of social housing, improving access to the Lachine Canal, and honouring the site's industrial heritage.

World.title: Judge dismisses sexual assault case against Trailer Park Boys star Mike Smith
World.content:
The audio version of this article is generated by AI-based technology. Mispronunciations can occur. We are working with our partners to continually review and improve the results.

A Nova Scotia judge dismissed a sexual assault case against Trailer Park Boys actor Mike Smith on Thursday, as the complainant tells CBC News she decided the emotional toll of testifying would be too difficult to endure.

The three-day trial of Smith, known for playing Bubbles on the comedy series, was set to begin on Thursday in provincial court in Dartmouth, N.S.

But the Crown offered no evidence in the case, so the defence requested the case be dismissed. Judge Jill Hartlen dismissed it.

Smith, 54, was charged in October 2025 with sexual assault in relation to an alleged assault on Dec. 30, 2017, in Dartmouth.

He pleaded not guilty to the charge in February.

CBC spoke with the complainant, who cannot be named due to a publication ban on her identity, on Wednesday.

In a statement, she said the trial was dismissed "because I am unwilling to sacrifice my mental he alth" by testifying.

The statement sa ys evidence in sexual assault cases "hinges almost exclusively on the testimony of the victim."

"This process retraumatizes survivors, subjecting their experiences to dissecting public scrutiny. Meanwhile, the accused seldom speak; they are exempt from the pain of taking the stand, giving testimony, and facing cross-examination," the statement reads.

Crown attorney Bryson McDonald speaks to reporters at provincial court in Dartmouth, N.S. on Thursday, Oct. 1, 2026. (Darren Calabrese/The Canadian Press)

Crown prosecutor Bryson McDonald declined to confirm Thursday that the complainant had refused to testify.

He told reporters he could not discuss private communications between the Crown and the complainant.

"The Crown made the assessment based on our prosecution standard that we felt that the realistic prospect of conviction was no longer there," McDonald said, noting that the determination was made this week.

The complainant said in her statement that since the burden of evidence in sexual assault cases relies so heavily on the character of the witness, victims face "character assassination" during cross-examinations, and defence lawyers can even "insinuate that victims played a part in the crime — or deserved it."

"I am intimidated by a system, despite it being 2026, where defence attorneys still use tactics that blame victims for surviving and reporting sexual assaults," the statement continues.

"I know what happened that night in 2017. My stepping away from the case does not change the facts of that incident. Rather, it is a gesture of reclaiming my agency after investigating options within a system that strips me of my voice."

The statement continues, "I also hope the legal system reflects on my words and implements equality in sexual assault cases, where both parties bear the burden of truth, rather than placing it solely on the person who has been harmed."

Stan MacDonald, the defence lawyer for actor Mike Smith, speaks to reporters at provincial court in Dartmouth, N.S., on Thursday, Oct. 1, 2026. (Darren Calabrese/The Canadian Press)

Smith’s defence lawyer, Stan MacDonald, said outside the courtroom that defence lawyers do not use tactics to try to dissuade complainants from testifying or to influence them.

Asked to respond to the notion that, generally, complainants sometimes don’t feel comfortable testifying because of scrutiny by defence lawyers and the risk of retraumatization during trial, MacDonald said, “we do what the law allows us to do within our ethical boundaries.”

MacDonald said Smith is "pleased that this matter is now behind him and he's ready to move forward."

A statement issued Thursday morning by Trailer Park Boys Incorporated said now that the court matter has concluded, Smith is resuming his responsibilities with the company. He had previously stepped away from his role as managing director.

World.title: Macklemore says Free Palestine tour 'sold out immediately'
World.content:
The audio version of this article is generated by AI-based technology. Mispronunciations can occur. We are working with our partners to continually review and improve the results.

Macklemore says all three shows of his newly announced tour to raise funds for organizations supporting Palestinians "sold out immediately."

This comes less than a week after the four-time Grammy winner announced the October dates in Dublin, Paris and London, calling it the Free Palestine tour.

Macklemore hasn't revealed who will be taking the stage with him yet. The initial post announcing the tour says the shows will feature the rapper "and friends." He said Wednesday that the lineups are "coming soon."

The rapper announced the three-show European run last week after being removed as an opener for the U.S. leg of English singer-songwriter Ed Sheeran's tour.

"I’m honestly blown away," Macklemore wrote on Instagram on Wednesday. "We put these shows together fast and in community, believing that musicians can stand in solidarity with Palestine, use the stage to raise funds and show what collective action can look like."

CBC News reached out to representatives for Macklemore about whether he'd be bringing shows to Canada, but has not heard back.

"Dublin, Paris and London, thank you for showing up the way you did," he added.

According to a press release from Live Nation, the shows will benefit several Palestinian aid organizations, including Gaza Soup Kitchen, Palestinian Youth Movement, Jewish Voice for Peace and UNRWA USA, the American committee of the UN agency dedicated to Palestinian refugees.

What led to this?

Macklemore was dropped from Sheeran's tour after the owners of several American venues threatened to cancel Sheeran's shows if the rapper continued as his opening act, according to a statement from Messina Touring Group, the promoter of the U.S. leg of the tour, to Rolling Stone magazine.

Sheeran later put out a statement and said that one of the people threatening to cancel was Robert Kraft, chairman and CEO of The Kraft Group, which owns Gillette Stadium in Foxboro, Mass., and several professional sports teams.

Macklemore has openly expressed pro-Palestinian views for years and has made similar remarks on different stages in the past.

WATCH | Ed Sheeran speaks on stage at first show since Macklemore controversy: Ed Sheeran admits 'mistakes' at first show since Macklemore controversy | Duration closed caption 1:58 Fans remain divided after Ed Sheeran's apology at his first show since Macklemore was dropped as an opening act from the tour over his 'Free Palestine' comments.

After Sheeran's statement, all other openers dropped out of his tour, including his backing band.

On stage in Philadelphia on Sept. 19 — the first show following the controversy —Sheeran addressed the situation, saying he "never wanted to be an activist musician."

The shows at Gillette Stadium were ultimately cancelled due to severe weather.

World.title: What we know so far about the midair FlyDubai attack
World.content:
The audio version of this article is generated by AI-based technology. Mispronunciations can occur. We are working with our partners to continually review and improve the results.

A co-pilot stabbed his captain in an apparent attempt to crash a flight bound for Israel from the United Arab Emirates on Wednesday that was carrying 174 people. The passengers, most of them Israelis, feared for their lives as the FlyDubai aircraft lost half its altitude in about a minute.

The wounded pilot managed to open the cockpit door, and a passenger and a crew member rushed in to subdue the attacker, according to Israeli officials and plane passengers. Other crew members gained control of the aircraft, which landed safely in Saudi Arabia.

Here's what we know, and what isn't known, so far:

The incident

The distress call came at 8:44 a.m. local time, about 2½ hours after Flight FZ1073 left Dubai, a hub of international business and tourism, heading to Tel Aviv in Israel.

Israeli officials later said that the co-pilot stabbed the pilot and tried to crash the aircraft.

The plane swiftly lost altitude — dropping from 33,000 feet to 17,000 feet (10,000 metres to 5,100 metres) in the span of about a minute. It then circled close to the Jordanian border before landing in Tabuk, Saudi Arabia, about an hour later.

Aviation experts said they were surprised that the plane did not crash after a descent so extreme that most of the rudder was ripped off the aircraft's tail.

How the mid-air struggle aboard a FlyDubai flight unfolded | Hanomansing Live | Duration closed caption 11:21 Passengers and crew aboard a FlyDubai flight regained control after a co-pilot attacked the pilot and sent the plane plunging nearly 4,200 metres in less than 30 seconds, Israeli officials say. Aviation analyst Mark Miller discusses what the reported damage to the aircraft suggests about the violence onboard.

Hours after the plane landed at Tabuk's Prince Sultan bin Abdulaziz International Airport, replacement aircraft retrieved the passengers, who arrived in Israel on Wednesday night.

The wounded pilot, Capt. Smit Machchhar, from Mumbai, has been praised for opening the cockpit door so that others could subdue the attacker and take control of the Boeing 737, pulling it out of a risky dive. Other crew members were able to fly the plane to a safe landing.

Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu said on X that the pilot's opening of the cockpit door had "enabled passengers and crew to overpower the attacker — preventing a catastrophic midair disaster."

The alleged attacker

The United Arab Emirates government said an investigation team had begun its work, adding that it has jurisdiction because the plane is registered there. The state news agency said the probe will try and determine, in part, "whether the incident was linked to any terrorist activity or ⁠purpose, or involved prior planning or direction."

Israeli intelligence and security officials were in Saudi Arabia to help investigate the suspect, according to a regional official who spoke to The Associated Press on condition of anonymity because they were not authorized to speak to the media. Israel has requested that the suspect be sent to Israel for the investigation, though it is unclear if that request will be granted, the official said.

Israeli officials have identified the attacker as an Omani national. Omani authorities have not commented.

Netanyahu said in an interview on Fox News on Thursday that the attacker had undergone "Islamist radical indoctrination," but did not provide further details to support that allegation.

The security questions

One question surrounding the incident is what was used in the attack — and if it was a knife, how a pilot could transport it onto the aircraft without being detected.

Pilots, like passengers, must pass through metal detectors at airports. It's also standard for airlines to check their pilots' background for criminal and employment history, and their physical and mental health, as well as having them undergo intelligence and security screening.

This screengrab taken from a handout video via AFP-TV shows passengers inside the rerouted FlyDubai Flight FZ1073. (AFPTV/AFP/Getty Images)

Netanyahu brought up the possibility in the Fox News interview that an axe was used. Airlines are generally required to carry crash axes in the cockpit for use in an emergency to break open a window to escape or break open a panel to access a fire.

The cockpit door on all aircraft is locked during flight for security reasons — a measure that became the industry standard after the Sept. 11, 2001, attacks, in which hijackers broke into the cockpits of four domestic flights in the United States.

Israel, targeted in a series of hijackings decades ago, has some of the most stringent airline security measures worldwide. Passengers on Israel-bound flights regularly are taken aside for questioning and baggage searches after passing through normal airport security.

The attacked pilot

Machchhar was in ​"good health and recovering ​well," the Indian ⁠Embassy ⁠in ‌the U.A.E. said Thursday on X.

The ⁠embassy said the Indian ambassador there visited the pilot in hospital and ​it remained ⁠in close co-ordination ⁠with local authorities ⁠to ⁠ensure ​his continued medical care ​and well-being.

Indian pilot Smit Machchhar, who the leaders of Israel and India hailed as a hero for saving passengers after he was attacked by his colleague in an alleged attempt to crash a FlyDubai plane on Wednesday, smiles in this undated handout image. (Israel Foreign Ministry/Reuters)

Speaking to the Times of Israel, a passenger named Dr. Shota Musaev, a dentist, said Machchhar was bleeding from the head and hands after the attack. Musaev said he helped stop the bleeding.

SpiceJet, a budget carrier in India, also praised Machchhar early Thursday. SpiceJet said he had been an employee of theirs for about a decade, with a LinkedIn profile attached to Machchhar indicating he started flying for FlyDubai in 2022.

Machchhar has logged nearly 9,750 flying hours over a career spanning about 15 years, according to a Reuters report. In a podcast interview published on YouTube last year, the captain said, "I always wanted to fly a Boeing. My first aircraft was a Boeing."

The airline and the plane

FlyDubai says it has more than 6,000 employees from 144 countries. While the airline doesn't break down those numbers by pilots, it said in 2024 that it was on a recruitment drive to hire 130 new pilots by the end of that year.

The airline, in operation for nearly 20 years, says it flies to more than 125 destinations in some 56 countries across Africa, Europe, Central Asia, the Gulf, the Middle East, the Indian subcontinent and Southeast Asia.

Its most tragic incident occurred in 2016, when all 62 passengers and crew aboard its Boeing 737-800 died in a nighttime crash on a second landing attempt in Russia. Pilot error was among the factors cited in the final report on the crash.

While the airline has ordered some Airbus planes for future use, its fleet at present includes dozens of Boeing 737 aircraft of various generations.

While Boeing has been under fire in the past decade regarding other aviation incidents, the American company was praised during this event by U.S. President Donald Trump on Truth Social.

"Congratulations to the GREAT Boeing company for producing a plane, the 737 Max, that was able to withstand the G Forces and Strain far beyond what it was designed and expected to. It was an amazing show of precise and powerful structural panning and design," he wrote.

World.title: Jim Carrey marries Min Ah months after going public with relationship
World.content:
The audio version of this article is generated by AI-based technology. Mispronunciations can occur. We are working with our partners to continually review and improve the results.

Canadian comedian Jim Carrey has tied the knot with Min Ah, the partner he introduced to the public back in February.

Carrey was accepting an honour at the César Film Awards in Paris, France, when he described Min Ah as his "sublime companion," telling her in French that he loved her and that she was an angel.



Carrey 64, is known for trying to keep his private life private, and very little is known about his mysterious new bride. Hello! magazine reports she is 32 years old, exactly half his age.

It also appears the pair have been dating for several years, as the website Just Jared published photos of them leaving a benefit show together in 2022.



Min and Carrey were wed in a small private ceremony in Los Angeles, according to TMZ. His spokesperson would only confirm to CBC News that the actor is married, and had no further comment.

This is Carrey's third marriage.

Jim Carrey poses for a photo with his daughter Jane, left, and grandson Jackson, right, at the 51st Cesar Film Awards in Paris, France. (Francois Durand/Getty Images)

He was married to Melissa Womer from 1987 to 1993. Together, they had one daughter, Jane Erin Carrey , who accompanied Min and Carrey to the César Film Awards, along with Carrey's grandson, Jackson.

In French, he told his family, "I love you. I love you now and forever."

In 1996, Carrey married Dumb and Dumber co-star Lauren Holly. She filed for divorce less than a year later.

Carrey dated Renee Zellweger after co-starring with her in Me, Myself, and Irene in 1999. The pair broke up in 2000, but 20 years later, he described her as his "last great love" in his book Memoirs and Misinformation.

Although they were never married, Carrey was in a long-term relationship with U.S. actor and model Jenny McCarthy from 2005 to 2010.

World.title: Colombia’s top corporate lobbyist resigns over reported tensions with president
World.content:
The director of one of Colombia’s most powerful business associations, Bruce Mac Master of the ANDI, resigned amid tensions with President Abelardo de la Espriella.

In a letter to the ANDI, Mac Master said that “it is time for me to step down from my role as head of the National Association of Entrepreneurs of Colombia.”

According to the former ANDI boss, “unexpected and troubling circumstances” made working for the association “particularly complex” and ‘multiple pressures have affected its ability to act freely and carry out its functions autonomously.”

In recent weeks, unexpected and troubling circumstances have arisen that have made the Association’s operating environment particularly complex, with potential adverse effects on its members and staff. Multiple pressures have affected its ability to act freely and carry out its functions autonomously. In the face of these challenges, I have sought to act with firmness and prudence, always prioritizing institutional channels and placing the interests of the ANDI above any personal considerations, in an effort to resolve this situation. Bruce Mac Master

Mac Master’s resignation followed news suggesting that De la Espriella instructed his cabinet of boycotting the ANDI chief.

According to political news magazine La Silla Vacia, the rift between the ANDI and the government was because De la Espriella’s law firm was never allowed to join the ANDI and the association’s donations in response to the august 10 earthquake bypassed the First Lady’s newly founded and very controversial foundation.

“The General Board of Directors, its Executive Committee, and I did everything in our power to facilitate a solution and create conditions that would allow the Association to fully fulfill its role, seeking to keep channels of dialogue open and to continue contributing,” but “all of those attempts were unsuccessful.”

I deeply regret this, because I have always believed in collective intelligence and in the need for the government, the private sector, and institutions to work together—even in the face of differences—with respect, independence, and a sense of national responsibility. We tried, but we were unsuccessful. Bruce Mac Master

Mac Master said that he hoped that his resignation would restore “collaboration between the national government and the business community—as represented by the General Board of Directors, the members, and the various divisions of the Association.”

The former ANDI chief had been trying to represent the business interests of its approximately 1,600 members since 2013.

World.title: Colombia seeks to tighten checks on public protests
World.content:
Colombia’s government published a draft decree that seeks to tighten regulations on public protests.

The draft was published weeks before labor unions and social organizations plan regional anti-government protests ahead of a national strike that is set for November.

The draft seeks to update the Decree #3 of 2021, which was issued months before a national strike that was violently repressed by the police and the military.

In an attempt to prevent another bloodbath, the decree seeks to regulate authorities’ response to protests and the coordinated use of force in response to acts of vandalism and violence.

The decree regulates dialogue between the protesters and law enforcement authorities to promote the peaceful nature of protests.

The decree additionally limits the use of police intelligence against those organizing and participating in the protests.

Last but not least, the decree seeks the effective prosecution of those arrested during protests through increased surveillance and a permanent police presence.

The decree comes amid social tensions that surged after the far-right President Abelardo de la Espriella took office in August and announced counterrevolutionary measures that seek to undo reforms by his leftist predecessor, former President Gustavo Petro.

Swelling student protests have been publicly accused of being fueled by insurgencies and De la Espriella has warned that police may enter universities if they find evidence they are used to prepare acts of vandalism or terrorism.

World.title: Colombia breaks diplomatic ties with Iran
World.content:
Colombia’s Foreign Ministry said Thursday that it had broken diplomatic ties with Iran and designated the Islamic Revolutionary Guard Corps (IRGC) as a terrorist organization.

The foreign ministry made the announcements in two separate statements that were published in its website.

In the first statement, the government claimed that the decision claimed to defend “national and hemispheric security, and the fight against transnational crime.”

According to the foreign ministry, the Iranian government has “alleged ties to international terrorist groups and other narco-terrorist groups that threaten [Colombia’s] security.”

Colombia also took into account the documented human rights violations committed by the Iranian government on its territory, the verified attacks against countries not involved in the Middle East conflict, the blockade of the Strait of Hormuz, and the authorities’ obstruction of the International Atomic Energy Agency’s (IAEA) efforts to verify the scope of Iran’s nuclear program. Foreign Ministry

In regards to the IRGC, the foreign ministry claimed that the Iranian armed force “poses a serious threat to international peace and security” through “covert operations beyond Iran’s borders.”

“Colombia will strengthen its control and security measures to prevent individuals associated with the IRGC from entering its territory,” said the foreign ministry in a second statement.

In his 2017 book “Watch Your Backyard,” Foreign Minister Omar Bula claimed that “Iran and Islamic extremist groups such a Hezbollah and Al Qaeda have profusely penetrated Latin America.”

As part of his foreign policy, President Abelardo de la Espriella has renewed ties with the United States, Israel and the United Arab Emirates.

In a response, the Iranian government said that the accusations of the De la Espriella government go “against the principles of mutual respect” and damage both countries’ “interests and benefits.”

“It is clear that none of the arguments put forward by the Colombian government to justify this decision are valid or logical, and that this measure was adopted solely under the influence of the Zionist regime and the United States,” said Iran’s foreign ministry.

World.title: ACSN extends lockdown of Colombia’s Caribbean coast to Friday morning
World.content:
Santa Marta-based organized crime group ACSN said Wednesday that the lockdown it has imposed on parts of Colombia’s Caribbean coast will be lifted on Friday morning.

In its first formal statement, the ACSN said that “the armed strike announced for 72 hours will end at 7:00AM on Friday 25 September 2026.”

The lockdown, which was initially called for 48 hours on Monday, has devastated the legal economy in the port city, particularly after ACSN assassins uploaded videos of them opening fire at stores that ignored the order to social media.

The online videos and half a dozen burnt buses and taxis all but cleared the streets of Santa Marta, which became a ghost town on Tuesday.

“We have never seen anything like this,” one Santa Marta resident told news program El Reporte Coronell.

President Abelardo de la Espriella announced the militarization of Santa Marta, but this was barely visible in the city’s downtown area and in the majority of Santa Marta’s neighborhoods.

“There are no police or soldiers in the streets, the people feel unprotected and are in panic,” said journalist Javier Manjarres on social media platform X.

“The current situation is a consequence of the behavior of the security forces and the decisions taken by the National Government in regards to our organization,” the organized crime group said in their statement.

The ACSN admitted that the clandestine lockdown was the result of the killing of Jose Luis Perez, a.k.a. “Cholo,” one of its commanders in the region around the Sierra Nevada mountain range just outside the city.

According to the group, security forces executed Cholo in front of his wife after his arrest.

An 18-year-old farmhand with no ties to the organization was also executed by the security, his family told media.

The lockdown has been imposed throughout the Magdalena and La Guajira provinces, a region where the group dominates organized crime and controls drug trafficking route to the Caribbean.

World.title: Colombia withdraws support for ICJ genocide case against Israel
World.content:
Colombia has withdrawn its participation in South Africa’s genocide case against Israel, the International Court of Justice (ICJ) said Tuesday.

In a statement, the court in The Hague said that Colombia’s government “decided to withdraw the Declaration of intervention that it had filed… on 5 April 2024 in the case concerning Application of the Convention on the Prevention and Punishment of the Crime of Genocide in the Gaza Strip.”

The decision of the administration of President Abelardo De la Espriella is part of a wider attempt to restore ties with Israel and its main sponsor, the United States, and appease its Evangelical Christian support base.

In response to the ongoing genocide in Palestine, former President Gustavo Petro took a leading role in diplomatic efforts that sought to isolate Israel and seek justice for Israel’s victims through the world court.

In a response, the US Government put Petro on a blacklist and actively campaigned for the election of De la Espriella to prevent another leftist victory in elections earlier this year.

The new president, who took office in August, immediately restored diplomatic ties to Israel and lifted a ban on coal exports to the country in West Asia.

World.title: ACSN crime group shuts down parts of Colombia’s Caribbean coast
World.content:
Santa Marta-based crime group ACSN shut down parts of the city and the surrounding region after Colombia’s armed forces killed one of their commanders.

Jose Luis Perez, a.k.a. “Cholo,” and six of his comrades were killed during an offensive on Monday.

The son of Fredy Castillo, a.k.a. “Pinocho,” who is one of the alleged bosses of the crime group, was reportedly among those killed during the operation.

Shortly after, a pamphlet that was signed by the ACSN ordered an “armed strike” of 48 hours because of the “the fierce attacks that the government has been launching against our organization in the Sierra Nevada since this afternoon.”

Multiple buses were incinerated in the region around Santa Marta.

We hereby declare a 48-hour armed strike throughout the province of Magdalena, particularly along the Troncal del Caribe highway, in the city of Santa Marta, and in the banana-growing region. We do not want any businesses to remain open for a period of 48 hours. ACSN

According to President Abelardo de la Espriella, who traveled to the city, “they are trying to intimidate the public by promoting an armed strike.”

“I will not allow any criminal organization to subjugate citizens through threats and terror,” the president added.

Notwithstanding, multiple shop owners in Santa Marta and along the highway kept their shops closed on Tuesday, afraid to challenge the authority of the local crime bosses.

The district government closed public schools in neighborhoods where the ACSN is believed to have a strong presence. Public transport was suspended as videos of armed men opening fire on shops that failed to close voluntarily were posted on social media.

The ACSN control much of drug trafficking to the port of Santa Marta and to the coastline of the neighboring La Guajira province.

De la Espriella ended attempts to negotiate the group’s surrender and ordered a military approach after taking office in August.

World.title: Colombia’s war crimes tribunal warns ICC that De la Espriella supports “worst attack in history”
World.content:
Colombia’s war crimes tribunal JEP said that it would warn the United Nations and the International Criminal Court about plans of President Abelardo de la Espriella to cut its budget.

In a statement, JEP president Alejandro Ramelli raised the alarm warned about a pending proposal by far-right Senator Enrique Gomez (National Salvation) to reduce the tribunal’s budget by COP100 billion ($31.6 million), which received De la Espriella’s support.

A second proposal by another far-right party, the Democratic Center, sought to push all sentences against members of the security forces to military justice for revision.

According to Ramelli, the two bill proposals “prove the existence of a strategy to block the JEP’s functioning” and called on the international community to “put a stop to this effort to dismantle our financial system and calls for the essential resources needed for our operations to be guaranteed.”

These initiatives constitute a combined strategy of economic strangulation and the subjugation of the JEP to military criminal justice. It is the most serious attack we have ever faced against our independence and autonomy. JEP president Alejandro Ramelli

The president , who vowed to get rid of the JEP on campaign, said that the 2027 national budget “does not constitute any threat to any judge, it’s the Constitution at work.”

I do not have a policy of retaliation against the JEP. I have a duty to manage spending, demand results, and allocate the State’s limited resources to a justice system that serves everyone, not to a court that part of the country perceives—for reasons debated in Congress and in public opinion—as a system of privileges rather than an effective end to impunity. President Abelardo de la Espriella

Since March of 2018, the JEP has played a key role in clarifying crimes committed during the armed conflict that erupted in response to the insurgency of the now-defunct guerrilla group FARC.

Among other things, the JEP found that the guerrillas recruited more than 18,000 children and that the security forces assassinated more than 7,800 civilians to inflate their combat kills.

Hundreds of former guerrillas and former members of the armed forces are taking part in a transitional justice system that seeks to solve as many as possible of the hundreds of thousands of crimes committed during the decades-long armed conflict.

World.title: Colombia pulls out of international LGBT coalition
World.content:
The government of President Abelardo de la Espriella pulled Colombia out of the international Equal Rights Coalition, which promotes the rights of sexual and gender minorities around the world.

The Foreign Ministry announced its departure from the coalition in a letter addressed to the organization of which Colombia was co-president until February next year.

According to Caribe Afirmativa, a gay rights NGO that was part of the international initiative, warned that the decision was “a serious setback in foreign policy and commitments to LGBTIQ+ rights.”

We also view this action as a snub to the international community, a break from the leadership role Colombia had established, and an unequivocal political signal regarding the place the current government is willing to grant to the rights of LGBTIQ+ people. Caribe Afirmativa

De la Espriella has appointed multiple prominent far-right figures in his government and has vowed to wage a “Culture War” against what it considers “gender ideology.”

On top of this, De la Espriella and multiple of his cabinet members oppose the right of gay couples to adopt children and reportedly sacked the newly appointed planning chief because he and his gay partner had adopted a child.

World.title: Uruguay's foreign minister separates the "invaded island" from the money extracted from the Falklands
World.content:
Uruguay's foreign minister separates the “invaded island” from the money extracted from the Falklands

1st Thursday, October 2026 - 09:32 UTC Full article

The minister said this was the main subject of his conversation with his Argentine counterpart, Pablo Quirno, and denied discussing with him Uruguay's interest in acquiring British ships

Uruguay's Foreign Minister Mario Lubetkin argued that the Falklands dispute has changed in nature with oil exploration: one thing, he said, is “the invaded island” and “the fight against colonialism”, and another is “when a lot of money is taken from there”. His remarks come as Yamandú Orsi's government considers buying two patrol vessels from the Royal Navy, a deal that has already prompted a resolution from twenty deputies of Argentine President Javier Milei's party.

“When the process of oil prospecting by the United Kingdom began in the islands, the whole logic of the Malvinas issue changed,” he said on Wednesday on Canal 10's Arriba Gente programme, referring to the economic use of a territory he described as “taken colonially”. “That means that behind it comes military articulation, because you will try to defend those funds,” he said, calling for a move to “another phase” that includes reflection by the political system. He also said Argentina “is defending its rights and its heritage”.

The minister said this was the main subject of his conversation with his Argentine counterpart, Pablo Quirno, and denied discussing with him Uruguay's interest in acquiring British ships.

The United Kingdom has offered Uruguay three first-generation River-class offshore patrol vessels — HMS Tyne, HMS Mersey and HMS Severn — of which the defence ministry hopes to acquire up to two. A navy mission visited the Mersey in London in May, and a transfer could take place in 2028, when the Royal Navy retires them. No final decision has been taken. The search follows the cancellation in October 2025 of a contract with Spanish shipyard Cardama for two patrol vessels, which the government rescinded after finding “strong indications” of fraud.

The Uruguayan navy has raised technical objections, including the lack of a helicopter hangar. Opposition senator Javier García, a former defence minister, called the deal “more political than technical” and warned of the signal it would send to Buenos Aires in the current context.

In Argentina, deputy Damián Arabia and 19 other La Libertad Avanza lawmakers filed a draft resolution expressing “bewilderment and concern” over the possible purchase. “Our fraternal ties and Uruguay's historic, supportive and generous backing for the Malvinas Cause warrant avoiding this acquisition,” he wrote. The resolution is non-binding and the Argentine government has not lodged an official protest.

The remarks come amid an escalation. On Monday Argentina announced arbitration against the United Kingdom over the Sea Lion oil project; British Overseas Territories Minister Uma Kumaran replied on Wednesday that such conduct “raises questions” about Argentina's reliability as a partner. The United Kingdom maintains that the activity is governed by the archipelago's legislation in accordance with international law. In the 2013 referendum, on a 92% turnout, 99.8% of voters chose to retain the status of a British overseas territory.

World.title: The Spectator likens Milei's Falklands push to Galtieri's
World.content:
The Spectator likens Milei's Falklands push to Galtieri's

30th Wednesday, September 2026 - 23:01 UTC Full article

An opinion column published on Wednesday in the British weekly The Spectator likens Argentine President Javier Milei's campaign over the Falklands to that of dictator Leopoldo Galtieri in 1982, with the difference, its author argues, that the current government is using legal rather than military means. The piece, by law professor Andrew Tettenborn, is an argument of opinion rather than a report of new facts.

The columnist calls “lawfare” — the use of legal instruments for political ends — the arbitration Argentina announced on Monday over the Sea Lion oil project. He argues that the real aim is to reopen the sovereignty question, that Milei sees the United Kingdom as weak and divided, and that he is seeking a distraction from domestic difficulties. These are the author's assessments; he also directs personal characterisations at British Prime Minister Andy Burnham and at Milei himself.

The legal core of the column is its most concrete part: the author argues that Argentina's claim is in substance a territorial sovereignty dispute and that the international law of the sea tribunal has made clear it does not see that as its role. In previous cases, tribunals constituted under the United Nations Convention on the Law of the Sea have declined to rule on sovereignty disputes, as in the 2015 arbitration between Mauritius and the United Kingdom over the Chagos Islands. The procedure Buenos Aires has announced is an Annex VII arbitration; from the Hamburg-based International Tribunal for the Law of the Sea, Argentina would only seek provisional measures while the arbitral tribunal is constituted.

The column contains inaccuracies. It places the environmental lawsuit against the project in Buenos Aires and suggests it was filed with Milei's tacit approval; it was filed on September 1, before the presidential address that launched the campaign, by the Falklands War Veterans Centre of La Plata and an association of environmental lawyers before the federal court in Río Grande, Tierra del Fuego. Nor is it confirmed that the criminal complaints cover Rockhopper executives, as the text states.

Tettenborn advises the British government to reject the claim and “hold our nerve”, and argues that international courts have lost impartiality. The British statement issued the same Wednesday, however, expressly invokes the Law of the Sea Convention as the legal framework for oil activity in the archipelago.

Argentina argues that unilateral exploitation contravenes UN General Assembly resolutions 2065 and 31/49 and that the residents' wishes do not settle the dispute. In the 2013 referendum, on a 92% turnout, 99.8% of voters chose to retain the status of a British overseas territory.

World.title: London rejects Argentina's arbitration and questions its "reliability" as a partner
World.content:
London rejects Argentina's arbitration and questions its “reliability” as a partner

30th Wednesday, September 2026 - 22:59 UTC Full article

MLA Roberts this morning working the Labour Party Conference with Minister of Overseas Territories and Defence Secretary Wes Streeting

The British government has rejected Argentina's decision to initiate international arbitration over the Sea Lion oil project and said Buenos Aires' campaign over the Falklands “raises questions about Argentina's reliability as a partner for the United Kingdom”. It is the first time London has extended the dispute to the bilateral relationship as a whole.

The statement, signed by Parliamentary Under-Secretary of State for the Overseas Territories Uma Kumaran and released on Wednesday, describes the recourse to the United Nations Convention on the Law of the Sea as “the latest attempt to undermine the rights and livelihoods” of the archipelago's residents. It says they “have freely and democratically chosen their future” and have the right to develop their natural resources “without intimidation, coercion or interference from others”, and that hydrocarbon activity is regulated under local law “in full accordance with international law, including UNCLOS”. These are UK government positions, contested by Argentina.

According to the text, London told Argentina's ambassador to the United Kingdom this week that efforts to obstruct economic activity “are not acts of responsible international engagement” but “deliberate attempts to undermine the prosperity and economic security of a self-governing people”. The statement concludes that the United Kingdom will continue to stand “shoulder-to-shoulder” with the archipelago's government and will “robustly defend” its wishes, its economy and its right to self-determination. On X, Kumaran wrote: “The Falkland Islands are British.” Rockhopper Exploration, the project's British partner, said it would press ahead with Sea Lion and called Argentina's claim “illegitimate”, according to the Buenos Aires Herald.

President Javier Milei on Monday ordered the start of arbitration proceedings under Annex VII of the Convention and gave London two weeks to prevent exploitation in the basin north of the archipelago; if it does not, Argentina will seek provisional measures from the Hamburg-based International Tribunal for the Law of the Sea. Buenos Aires argues that unilateral exploitation contravenes General Assembly resolutions 2065 and 31/49 and causes “irreversible and irreparable” harm to its rights. In previous cases, tribunals under the Convention have declined to rule on territorial sovereignty disputes.

Argentina also has 60 administrative proceedings open, with no penalty applied, and three criminal complaints against ten companies. None of the allegations has been proven. In the 2013 referendum, on a 92% turnout, 99.8% of voters chose to retain the status of a British overseas territory.

World.title: Trump and six tech companies sign a voluntary artificial intelligence safety accord
World.content:
Trump and six tech companies sign a voluntary artificial intelligence safety accord

30th Wednesday, September 2026 - 19:10 UTC Full article

The document, titled “White House Accord on Super Intelligence: Joint Commitment on Frontier Responsibilities”, was posted by the president after a lunch with industry executives

US President Donald Trump and the heads of six technology companies signed a voluntary accord at the White House on Tuesday under which the companies commit to ensuring the safety of their own artificial intelligence systems. Trump called it “morally binding” and said it was “almost like a constitution”.

The document, titled “White House Accord on Super Intelligence: Joint Commitment on Frontier Responsibilities”, was posted by the president on his Truth Social network after a lunch with industry executives. It was signed by Sundar Pichai of Google, Dario Amodei of Anthropic, Mark Zuckerberg of Meta, Greg Brockman of OpenAI, Jensen Huang of Nvidia and Elon Musk.

According to the text, the companies are responsible for the safety of their own technology, will implement safeguards so models operate as intended, will quickly detect and fix problems and will work with independent auditors to verify their systems do not access other technical systems in unintended ways. The accord sets no consequences for breaches. Trump also announced a board to oversee the area, without naming its members, and the appointment of a government official to lead on the issue in the coming days.

Zuckerberg described it as “a start”; Pichai as “historic and consequential”; and Amodei as a way “to win safely”. Specialists consulted by the BBC were critical. Kimberlee Weatherall, a law professor at the University of Sydney, said the accord lets companies “define what counts as safety” and called it “deeply unimpressive”. Jeannie Paterson of the University of Melbourne warned that self-regulation could mean “only minimal safeguards”.

The accord comes amid calls from parts of the industry and from experts for tighter oversight of the technology. According to the BBC, OpenAI cancelled the release of one of its models on Monday over safety concerns.

The same day, Trump signed an executive order requiring federal agencies to replace “artificial intelligence” with “Super Intelligence” or “SI” in official correspondence, websites and reports, and tasking his science and technology adviser with proposing a legal definition within 60 days. In his address to the UN General Assembly last week, the president said the word “artificial” made the technology “sound fake”.

Trump reiterated his support for the expansion of data centres, whose construction has become a sensitive issue ahead of November's midterm elections: a Marist poll for NPR and PBS found 65% of registered voters oppose having them built in their area.

The accord puts into practice the position Washington set out in New York against calls for common rules. There, British Prime Minister Andy Burnham called for “a single set of global principles and standards”, while Trump and Argentine President Javier Milei rejected any pre-emptive regulation.

World.title: Pilot stabs another on a Dubai–Tel Aviv flight and passengers subdue him
World.content:
Pilot stabs another on a Dubai–Tel Aviv flight and passengers subdue him

30th Wednesday, September 2026 - 18:10 UTC Full article

The pilot identified as the attacker has been arrested and is being questioned by Saudi authorities, according to Netanyahu

A pilot on a Flydubai flight from Dubai to Tel Aviv stabbed another pilot in the cockpit on Wednesday and, according to Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu, “apparently tried to crash the plane”. Passengers and crew members subdued him, and the aircraft made an emergency landing in Tabuk, in north-west Saudi Arabia, with all 174 passengers safe, 166 of them Israelis.

Flight FZ1073, a Boeing 737 MAX, had taken off from Dubai at 03:05 GMT. Near the Israel–Jordan border it first declared a general emergency and, minutes later, transmitted the unlawful interference code used in hijackings. According to Netanyahu, the aircraft lost about 5,200 metres of altitude in under two minutes before diverting. It landed in Tabuk at 06:58 GMT. The Israeli Air Force sent fighter jets towards the aircraft.

Netanyahu said he had spoken with a passenger who, together with a crew member, broke into the cockpit and overpowered the pilot “while he was attempting to sabotage the aircraft's systems”; another crew member stabilised the plane. Flydubai said the aircraft was secured by on-duty crew travelling on the flight, who diverted and landed it. The pilot identified as the attacker has been arrested and is being questioned by Saudi authorities, according to the prime minister. Israel's ambassador to the UN, Danny Danon, identified the injured pilot as Emirati.

Imagens de passageiros capturam o pânico a bordo de um voo da Flydubai após o co-piloto esfaquear o piloto, levando a aeronave a uma descida rápida de 17.000 pés. Passageiros correram em direção à cabine de pilotagem enquanto o co-piloto omanense começou a esfaquear o piloto.… — FREE BUBBLE (@FreeBubble40637) September 30, 2026

Israeli Defence Minister Israel Katz called the incident an “attempted jihadist terror attack”. The airline said the motives “are unknown” and subject to a formal investigation, and urged people to “refrain from premature speculation”. No authority has announced charges.

Several passengers said the plane began to drop and that screams came from the cockpit before three to five men went in to subdue the attacker. All were flown out on a replacement aircraft sent by Flydubai, which landed in Tel Aviv in the afternoon.

The incident comes weeks before Israel's elections. National Security Minister Itamar Ben-Gvir called it a terror attack; opposition leaders Yair Lapid and Avigdor Liberman accused the government's camp of seeking political advantage. Transport Minister Miri Regev called for Flydubai flights to be suspended. Former Israeli ambassador to the United Arab Emirates Amir Hayek urged instead that the airline be allowed to investigate, and President Isaac Herzog said Israel would keep acting “together with our Emirati partners”.

Flydubai operates ten daily flights in each direction between Dubai and Tel Aviv, a route opened after the 2020 Abraham Accords, under which the UAE recognised Israel.

World.title: Foundering of Argos Georgia with the loss of 13 lives, MAIB report points to hatch failure
World.content:
Foundering of Argos Georgia with the loss of 13 lives, MAIB report points to hatch failure

30th Wednesday, September 2026 - 07:29 UTC Full article

Image of Argos Georgia. (Courtesy of Argos Froyanes Limited)

Argos Georgia sinking, air photo from MOD

The marine accident investigation report refers to the loss of Argos Georgia, 23 July 2024, which occurred approximately 190 nautical miles east of Port Stanley. The Accident Investigation report 19/2026 includes what happened, subsequent actions taken and recommendations.

Argos Georgia was a longline fishing vessel registered in St Helena. The vessel foundered while on passage from Port Stanley in the Falkland Islands to fishing grounds near the island of South Georgia. Of the 27 people on board, 13 lost their lives.

The investigation found that the line hauling hatch in the starboard side of Argos Georgia opened unexpectedly. This allowed significant quantities of water to enter the vessel, causing it to list to starboard and founder.

Safety issues



• Cause of loss: The manual securing mechanism for the line hauling hatch had likely not been applied and the hatch could not be closed by the crew. This led to the vessel progressively flooding, loss of stability and foundering.

• Technical and operational failures: The hatch’s drive mechanism had an unidentified design weakness, while open weathertight doors, vulnerable electrical systems and inaccessible manual controls allowed flooding to spread.

• On board emergency response: The crew’s response was unstructured, and delays in declaring distress and abandoning ship reduced rescue time. Poor evacuation control, extreme conditions and liferaft damage increased cold water exposure and loss of life.

• Shoreside management deficiencies: The company lacked effective systems for controlling safety-critical risks and for assessing, escalating and responding to flooding, abandonment and distress emergencies in severe weather and remote waters.

Recommendations

The Maritime and Coastguard Agency is recommended to amend Merchant Shipping Notice 1873 (F) – The Code of Practice for the Construction and Safe Operation of Fishing Vessels of 24m Registered Length and Over – to include design requirements for shell door arrangements that, as a minimum, require automatic locking arrangements capable of securing doors in the closed position.

Argos Froyanes Limited is recommended to implement a documented safety management system across its fishing vessels.

The Falkland Islands Government, Directorate of Emergency Services and Islands Security is recommended to enhance the Falkland Islands maritime search and rescue communications capability so that direct and reliable contact can be established with vessels in distress within the Falkland Islands maritime search and rescue area of responsibility.

Falklands Legislator meets PM Burnham and cabinet members at Liverpool

World.title: Milei opens Argentina Week at the OECD and will meet Macron at the Élysée
World.content:
Milei opens Argentina Week at the OECD and will meet Macron at the Élysée

29th Tuesday, September 2026 - 21:50 UTC Full article

Friday will feature panels on energy and critical minerals, technology, artificial intelligence, international trade and fisheries. Milei will also receive an award from the Paris Economic Forum.

Argentine President Javier Milei will lead Argentina Week in Paris from Wednesday, a gathering aimed at attracting European investment, with its main day on Thursday at the headquarters of the Organisation for Economic Co-operation and Development, ending that evening with a private meeting with French President Emmanuel Macron at the Élysée Palace.

The schedule released by the Argentine presidency opens on Wednesday with a welcome reception at the embassy. On Thursday, at the Château de la Muette, Milei will deliver the keynote address under the theme “Forces driving Argentina's growth: milestones and investment opportunities”, following a panel on the country's macroeconomic transformation led by Economy Minister Luis Caputo and Central Bank Governor Santiago Bausili. He will then meet provincial leaders and a group of business executives. The meeting with Macron is scheduled for 6:50 p.m., followed at 8 p.m. by a reception hosted by the French president for the delegation. The two leaders met in Paris, Buenos Aires and Nice between 2024 and 2025.

Friday will feature panels on energy and critical minerals, technology, artificial intelligence, international trade and fisheries. Milei will also receive an award from the Paris Economic Forum.

Twelve governors are travelling — from Neuquén, Mendoza, Corrientes, Chubut, Río Negro, Santa Cruz, Salta, Jujuy, San Juan, Catamarca, Entre Ríos and Chaco — along with Buenos Aires city head of government Jorge Macri. Santa Fe's Maximiliano Pullaro is not attending. The national delegation includes Presidential General Secretary Karina Milei, Cabinet Chief Diego Santilli, Foreign Minister Pablo Quirno and ministers Federico Sturzenegger, Mario Lugones and Juan Bautista Mahiques.

Participants include TotalEnergies chief executive Patrick Pouyanné; ENI's Claudio Descalzi; Glencore's Gary Nagle; Santander's Héctor Grisi; Louis Dreyfus Company chair Margarita Louis-Dreyfus; YPF's Horacio Marín; and International Energy Agency executive director Fatih Birol. Vaca Muerta, liquefied natural gas, lithium and mining are at the centre of Argentina's pitch.

Before the trip, Milei told the weekly Le Point that French investors were welcome “to come and fill their pockets in Argentina” and said his government “sanctifies property rights and the sanctity of contracts”. In a separate interview with the channel LCI, he said “Europe is sinking”.

The trip comes as financial indicators deteriorate: country risk rose above 640 points on Monday, its highest level of the year, in the same week the president questioned official activity and poverty statistics.

World.title: Mexico in Numbers: Health and healthcare
World.content:
Last week we published Part 1 of the MND Mexico Well-being Series, which focused on eight health and healthcare indicators, including life expectancy, health expenditure per capita and hospital beds per 1,000 people.

This “Mexico in Numbers” article is a condensed version of that report — a concise presentation of the key data, complemented by visual features.

As we noted last week, the MND Mexico Well-being Series — a collection of articles on a range of topics related to well-being — will draw on the most recent internationally comparable data, as well as data from the past decade, to assess what has changed in Mexico during the eight years that the ruling Morena party has been in office.

A “Mexico in Numbers” companion piece will complement each article in the series.

Without further ado, let’s take a look at the key data from Part 1 of the series.

* The data in Part 1 of the MND Mexico Well-being Series, and hence the data in this article, comes from the OECD’s Health at a Glance 2025 report. The OECD report includes health and healthcare data for the 38 OECD countries, as well as OECD partner and accession countries in some cases.

Life expectancy at birth

Mexico’s life expectancy rose only marginally, from 75 years in 2015 to 75.5 years in 2024, leaving it 5.6 years below the OECD average of 81.1 years. In 2024, Mexico ranked 46th of 49 countries on this measure.

Avoidable mortality

Mexico recorded 418 avoidable deaths per 100,000 people in 2023 — almost twice the OECD average of 222 — to rank 40th of 44 countries, or fifth worst. Its preventable mortality rate rose about 10% between 2013 and 2023 to 243 deaths per 100,000 people, while the treatable mortality rate increased about 15% to 175.

Obesity

Some 36% of Mexicans aged 15 and over are obese, 10 percentage points above the OECD average of 26% and the second-highest rate among the 14 countries with measured data, behind only the United States (41%). Mexico’s obesity rate has risen from 33.3% in 2015, although its combined overweight-and-obesity rate has remained broadly stable at above 70% over the past decade.

Healthcare coverage

Mexico provided coverage for a core set of health services to 78% of its population in 2023, 20 percentage points below the OECD average of 98% and the lowest rate among 40 countries assessed. Coverage has deteriorated over the past decade, falling from 92.3% in 2015.

Health expenditure as a % of GDP

Mexico spent 5.9% of GDP on health care in 2024, 3.4 percentage points below the OECD average of 9.3%, ranking 42nd of 49 countries. Spending rose only marginally from 5.8% of GDP in 2016.

Health expenditure per capita

Mexico spent US$1,588 per person on health care in 2024, compared with an OECD average of US$5,967, which is 275% higher. Mexico ranked 43rd of 49 countries on this measure. Although real per-capita spending grew at an annual average of 2.1% between 2019 and 2024, Mexico’s spending gap with the OECD average widened slightly from 2016.

Hospital beds

Mexico had just 1 hospital bed per 1,000 people in 2023, compared with an OECD average of 4.2, ranking last among 44 countries assessed. The ratio was unchanged from a decade earlier.

Satisfaction with healthcare availability

In 2023, 56% of Mexicans said they were satisfied with the availability of quality healthcare where they live, eight percentage points below the OECD average of 64%. Mexico ranked 27th among 38 countries. Satisfaction increased only marginally from 55% in 2014.
