World.title: Punjab CM Mann says Rs 1,262 crore Satkar Rashi released to 36.87 lakh women
World.content:
Punjab CM Mann says Rs 1,262 crore Satkar Rashi released to 36.87 lakh women.

Join conversation View All Comments â Share your thoughts in the comments Insightful Agree Disagree Skeptical Concerning Promising Worth Reading Big Development Post Comment Be respectful Â· TOI community guidelines

Punjab Chief Minister Bhagwant Singh Mann on Thursday said Rs 1,262.54 crore was being transferred directly into the bank accounts of 36.87 lakh women under the state governmentâs Mawan Dheeyan Satkar Yojna.The amount constitutes the second instalment under the scheme and covers October, November and December, Mann said while addressing a function at Khandoor Sahib. Each beneficiary would receive the three-month instalment together, he said.According to Mann, Rs 2,562.33 crore had previously been distributed among 73.99 lakh women. With the latest disbursement, the total amount transferred under the scheme has reached Rs 3,824.87 crore, he said.Mann said around 97% of women in Punjab would be eligible for the scheme and that the government had set a target of extending its benefits to one crore women. He also said there were no conditions limiting the number of eligible women in a household, meaning that if three women in a family qualified, all three could receive the assistance.The chief minister said 1.37 lakh Satkar Sakhis had helped register women under the scheme and had received more than Rs 51 crore in incentives.Anganwadi workers involved in facilitating registrations would also receive incentives totalling Rs 25 crore, he said.At the event, Mann also criticised opposition parties and said that if the Congress, BJP or Akali Dal came to power, schemes including the Satkar Yojna, free bus travel for women and free electricity would be discontinued. These were political claims made by the chief minister.Mann also targeted the Congress and Shiromani Akali Dal, commenting on their internal political situation. He said the Congress had fewer workers but more leaders aspiring to become chief minister and alleged that the Akali Dal had misused religion.Referring to the state government's performance since 2022, Mann claimed that Punjab had moved from 27th to first position in school education according to the Centre's assessment. He said the government had established smart classrooms, trained teachers and recruited non-teaching staff.On medical education, Mann said around 30 lakh students appear for NEET every year and claimed that the number of students from Punjab's government schools clearing the examination had risen from 80 when he took office to 882 this year. He said the state had introduced free coaching for government-school students.Mann also said the government would open new centres for UPSC preparation to help students from Punjab prepare for the civil services.On power supply, the chief minister said eligible households were receiving 300 units of free electricity each month. He also said the state government had purchased the Goindwal Sahib Thermal Power Plant for Rs 1,080 crore.Mann said farmers were receiving daytime electricity for agricultural use and claimed that 14,000 kilometres of pipelines had been laid to take canal water to fields.He also said the pace of development in Punjab would increase between 2027 and 2032 as projects undertaken during the current government's tenure begin to show results.Cabinet minister Harbhajan Singh ETO and others were present at the event.

World.title: 17 Indian fishermen rescued by Seychelles, India expresses gratitude
World.content:
India has conveyed heartfelt thanks to Seychelles for the heroic rescue of 17 fishermen stranded at sea due to engine failure on the IFB Sajira.

NEW DELHI: India on Thursday showed gratitude to the Seychelles government for providing "swift and life-saving assistance" to 17 Indian fishermen on a fishing vessel that had an engine failure in the rough seas off the nation's coast.Ministry of external affairs spokesperson Randhir Jaiswal, said on X that the prompt aid demonstrated the "close and enduring bonds of friendship" between the two nations.He also included some pictures of the fishermen and the recovered fishing boat in his tweet."Government of India expresses gratitude to the Government of Seychelles for its swift and life-saving assistance to 17 Indian fishermen aboard IFB Sajira, which suffered an engine failure in the high seas off the coast of Seychelles," MEA said."This timely assistance reflects the close and enduring bonds of friendship between India and Seychelles, and our shared commitment to the safety and well-being of our people," he wrote.

World.title: ‘15,000 voters targeted’: Rahul Gandhi’s fresh attack on EC over Karnataka rolls
World.content:
NEW DELHI: Lok Sabha leader of opposition

on Thursday launched a scathing attack on the Election Commission and accused it of erasing nearly 15,000 voters from electoral rolls in Karnatakaâs Belagavi region.

In a social media post on X, Rahul said that a massive âfloodâ of Form 7 applications was filed in bulk over three days to remove targeted groups from the voter list.

âIn just three days - September 22, 23, and 24 - there was a flood of Form 7 applications to remove nearly 15,000 voters... Muslims, SCs, STs, and OBCs are being systematically targeted because they do not vote for the BJP,â Rahul said.

âI had already exposed this method of vote theft - votes are deleted through software in a centralised manner.

âSelectâ people are targeted as BJP and EC officials collude to fill out Form 7 in bulk through automated means - and in the blink of an eye, millions vanish from the voter list. And all of this is controlled from the top,â he added.

The Congress leader also demanded that Chief Election Commissioner Gyanesh Kumar immediately take action or step down, alleging that refusal to register an FIR undermines democratic institutions.





âKarnataka Congress leaders are at this moment demanding an FIR against the culprits at the Karnataka CEOâs office. Why is the CEO refusing this FIR? In this way, Modi, Shah, and Gyanesh are collectively destroying democracy through SIR. This is treason. That's why I'm saying Gyanesh Kumar should resign and become an approver, and there should be an investigation against Modi and Shah,â he added.

Form 7 is the official document prescribed by the Election Commission for objecting to the inclusion of or seeking the deletion of a name from an existing electoral roll.

In Belagavi, local election officials reportedly received thousands of such applications over a span of 72 hours, triggering alarm among local Congress workers and booth-level officers (BLOs).

Meanwhile, the poll panel and regional authorities clarified the procedural safeguards surrounding Form 7 filings. Election officials stressed that no voterâs name can be deleted automatically or solely based on the submission of a Form 7.

Every application requires physical field verification, notices to be issued to the affected voter, and due process to be conducted by Booth Level Officers (BLOs) before any deletion is finalised, the panel said.

Election officials instructed local BLOs to halt the immediate processing of suspected bulk filings and initiated internal inquiries to trace the origin of the submissions and verify whether the signatures were genuine.

World.title: VHP leader killing: NIA arrests UAE-deported fugitive Harwinder Kumar accused of  providing funding, logistics
World.content:
NEW DELHI: The National Investigation Agency (NIA) on Thursday arrested deported fugitive Harwinder Kumar @ Sonu, accused in the case related to the targeted killing of VHP leader Vikas Prabhakar in 2024, from the UAE.

Soon after landing at the Indira Gandhi International Airport here, he was placed under arrest by the NIA and later produced before the Special NIA court.

Harwinder, who was based in the UAE and on the NIA's 'wanted' list, was allegedly involved in providing logistical support and financing to foreign-based perpetrators of the crime, affiliated with pro-Khalistan terrorist outfit Babbar Khalsa International (BKI).

Prabhakar alias Vikas Bagga was shot dead in his confectionery shop at Nangal in Punjab's Roopnagar district on April 13, 2024. He was the Nangal president of the Vishva Hindu Parishad (VHP).

The NIA took over the case from the state police on May 9. Investigation has found that Prabhakar was killed by members of the Babbar Khalsa International, as part of conspiracy hatched by Germany-based BKI operatives Harjit Singh alias Laddi and Kulbeer Singh alias Sidhu.





Three chargesheets have been filed so far in the matter.

NIA on Thursday said Harwinder was deported from the UAE to India after vigorous diplomatic efforts. His arrest follows that of another UAE-based accused, Manveer Ram, on Aug 13, 2026. Manveer, allegedly involved in supplying weapons used in the crime, was intercepted at Amritsar Airport and subsequently arrested by the NIA.

NIA said Harwinder acted as both a recruiter and handler, arranged weapons and facilitated their delivery to the shooters involved in the killing Prabhakar.

He also received and transferred terror funds in connection with the conspiracy, acting on the directions of Harjit Singh and Kulbeer Singh.

"The deportation of Harwinder from the UAE and his subsequent arrest by the NIA demonstrate the agencyâs resolve to pursue fugitives involved in terrorism cases and bring them back to India to face the due process of law," NIA noted in its statement on Thursday.

World.title: Full-body scanners at airports: Govt tests tech & algorithms to address privacy concerns before wider rollout
World.content:
NEW DELHI: India's aviation security regulator is collecting data from ongoing trials of full-body scanners at Bengaluru and Cochin airports before deciding on their wider deployment, with the technology's algorithms also being refined to account for objects commonly worn by passengers in India.

Bureau of Civil Aviation Security (BCAS) Director General Rajesh Nirwan told reporters on Thursday that full-body scanners have been mandated at eight airports, while trials are currently being conducted at Bengaluru and Cochin. Authorities are collecting data from the trials, including the number of alarms generated, which will be assessed before a decision is taken on introducing the scanners at airports.

However, Cochin is not among the eight airports where the scanners have been mandated.

The deployment of full-body scanners has been delayed for years, partly due to concerns over passenger privacy. Nirwan said newer scanners are being made âimage agnosticâ, meaning they do not produce an actual image of the passenger but instead display a model and identify the specific part of the body where a suspicious object may have been detected, reported PTI.





BCAS is also working with scanner vendors and original equipment manufacturers to refine the technology for Indian conditions, including concerns that jewellery and other commonly worn items could trigger alarms.

âWhat we are getting today in India is based on algorithms that have been designed for foreign markets. There are certain typical things that are on the body of Indian citizens or people living in India.

So, those algorithms are also being continuously refined,â Nirwan said.

The data collected during the ongoing trials will be used to further refine the algorithms, he added.

Meanwhile, the officials also addressed the recent Flydubai cockpit attack in which Indian pilot Smit Machchhar was injured, saying Indian aviation authorities are examining the incident and will hold internal deliberations on whether any aviation security advisory is required.

Civil Aviation Secretary Samir Kumar Sinha said the matter was under examination and any decision on an advisory would be taken after internal discussions. â... in case some advisory is to be issued, obviously we will put it up to the higher authorities for taking a decision on that,â Sinha said.

The comments came a day after Flydubai flight FZ1073, flying from Dubai to Tel Aviv with 174 passengers, was diverted to Saudi Arabia after an altercation in the cockpit. Indian captain Smit Machchhar was seriously injured while trying to tackle his co-pilot, and the aircraft later landed safely at Tabuk.

World.title: New liquor shops in Bengal must maintain 500-metre gap from schools, religious places
World.content:
In a bid to regulate the liquor trade, the West Bengal government has raised the distance criteria for new liquor outlets from educational institutions and places of worship.

The West Bengal government has increased the necessary distance for new retail liquor outlets from educational institutions and holy places to 500 meters in urban and municipal areas and 1 km in other parts of the state, up from the former 300 meters, as per PTI.As per the recent notification given by the government, no new liquor licenses would be given within a 1 km distance of religious institutions, schools, and universities in rural and non-municipal areas, state Liquor Association Secretary Bijan Patra stated on Thursday.The government has kept the minimum distance at 500 meters from the religious places, schools, and educational insititutions for the areas under the Kolkata Municipal corporation (KMC) and other civic authorities, Bijan Patra added.However, he stated that Rule 8's distance requirements won't apply if an existing liquor store wishes to "shift" to a mall of any size.The prior framework required a minimum distance of 1,000 feet, or around 300 meters.Chief minister Suvendu Adhikari had already announced that his administration will not enable liquor sales within a 1 km radius of schools, universities, and shrines.Over 4,000 bars, off-shops, and liquor stores now operate within a 1-kilometer radius of these sensitive zones throughout the state; however, this new restriction will not affect already-existing establishments.In order to establish new offshops through bars, the new strategy also makes use of Section 4P of the excise act.However, some business owners have voiced reservations about the provision, claiming that because the state agency would keep a profit, it could not be advantageous for the liquor sector.

World.title: Government revises FASTag guidelines for Divyangjan category
World.content:
The government on Thursday revised guidelines for vehicles registered under the Divyangjan category. The beneficiaries will receive an exempted FASTag based on the disability percentage shown on their disability certificate, Unique Disability ID (UDID) card or other applicable records.

The Ministry of Road Transport and Highways revised the guidelines for issuing and renewing exempted FASTags for eligible beneficiaries to promote ease of living for citizens and further simplify toll-related procedures for Divyangjan and persons with disabilities (PwD).

Earlier, guidelines mandated renewal of exempted FASTags for Divyangjan on an annual basis.

However, under the new guidelines, the exempted FASTag’s validity will be determined by the percentage of disability.

FASTags issued to persons with 70% to 100% disability will be valid for five years, while those issued to persons with 40% to less than 70% disability will be valid for three years, the Ministry said.

According to the Ministry, the exempted FASTag may be renewed thereafter, subject to continued eligibility and compliance with the provisions of the National Highways Fee Rules, 2008.

The revised provisions are aimed at making the National Highway tolling ecosystem more accessible, transparent and user-friendly for eligible beneficiaries, while ensuring that toll exemptions continue to be administered in accordance with the prescribed rules and eligibility requirements.

World.title: Hindu College Staff Association flags ‘lapses’ in administration, urges DU V-C to take over
World.content:
The Hindu College Staff Association (HCSA) on Thursday submitted a memorandum to Delhi University Vice-Chancellor Yogesh Singh urging him to take over the college’s administration.

The association also sought an independent and time-bound inquiry into alleged irregularities in admissions, finances, procurement and appointments, and the college’s functioning. It alleged that there were irregularities in supernumerary admissions despite objections from teachers-in-charge and committee conveners.

It claimed that norms such as the prescribed 20% cap and applicable university ordinances had been breached. It also claimed that a meeting to ratify the admissions was presented as a staff council meeting even though no such meeting had been convened or attended by HCSA members.

The development comes against the backdrop of a controversy over admissions under the extracurricular activities and sports categories.

Show-cause notices

Last week, the association stated that three of its members were served show-cause notices even as they were “legitimately representing the collective and unanimous mandate of HCSA meetings”.

Principal Anju Srivastava had said the notices were issued in view of a “derogatory e-mail” sent by the staff members.

The memorandum alleged that faculty members were being denied leave, sabbaticals, and promotions.

It also raised concerns over the “repeated incidents of fire, structural defects, and seepage” in newly constructed buildings at the college.

University officials did not respond to requests for comment on the issue.

(With inputs from PTI)

World.title: 683 kg prohibited firecrackers seized in Rohini, three arrested
World.content:
The Delhi Police have arrested three men and seized 683 kg of prohibited firecrackers allegedly being stored and transported illegally in Rohini, officials said on Thursday.

The accused have been identified as Ravi, 35, a resident of Vijay Vihar Phase-II, and Ram Kumar, 47, and Chand, 49, both residents of Avantika in Sector 1, Rohini.

The arrests followed a raid at a godown in Budh Vihar, where the three men were allegedly found loading firecrackers into a car and a scooter, the police said.

The firecrackers were seized from the godown, and the two vehicles allegedly being used to transport them were also seized.

A case has been registered at the Budh Vihar police station under relevant sections of the Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita and Section 9(B) of the Explosives Act.

Further investigation was under way to ascertain the source of the firecrackers and identify others involved in their storage, supply and transportation.

World.title: SCCL registers growth in coal transportation, prioritises Telangana power plants
World.content:
Singareni Collieries Company Limited (SCCL) recorded significant growth in coal transportation during the first half of the current financial year ending September 30, supplying higher quantities of coal to consumers and thermal power stations across Telangana.

The SCCL transported 299.4 lakh tonnes of coal during the first six months of the current financial year, compared to 287.6 lakh tonnes during the corresponding period last year, registering a growth of 4%.

Reflecting its focus on meeting the State’s energy needs, SCCL supplied 198.2 lakh tonnes of coal to Telangana’s thermal power stations, a 24.58% increase over the 159.1 lakh tonnes supplied during the same period last year.

Among individual plants, coal supply to Kothagudem Thermal Power Station rose from 26.4 lakh tonnes to 39.8 lakh tonnes, a growth of 50.76%. Supplies to Yadadri Thermal Power Station increased by 57.67% from 21.5 lakh tonnes to 33.9 lakh tonnes, while Bhadradri Thermal Power Station received 24.4 lakh tonnes, up 25.13% from 19.5 lakh tonnes last year.

Coal transportation to Singareni Thermal Power Station stood at 26.6 lakh tonnes, registering a growth of 27.27%. Supplies to NTPC Telangana increased from 19.4 lakh tonnes to 25.3 lakh tonnes. However, coal supplies to NTPC Ramagundam marginally declined to 42.7 lakh tonnes from 43.5 lakh tonnes during the corresponding period last year.

The SCCL attributed the enhanced supplies to special measures taken in view of El Nino conditions and the need to ensure uninterrupted power generation in Telangana. Acting on directions from the State and Central governments, the company coordinated closely with power sector agencies to boost coal production and transportation.

SCCL Chairman and Managing Director Dr. Buddhaprakash Jyoti has been reviewing production and transportation targets on a daily basis with area general managers, while five senior officials have been assigned to monitor coal movement to thermal power stations.

Dr. Jyoti said SCCL considers meeting Telangana’s power requirements a responsibility beyond commercial considerations and is working in a planned manner to achieve its annual targets of 620 lakh tonnes of coal production and 650 lakh tonnes of coal transportation.

World.title: Govt. caps sugar stock limit for dealers to 1,000 quintals ahead of festive season
World.content:
The government on Thursday (October 1, 2026) tightened the stock-holding limit for sugar dealers to 1,000 quintals, effective from October 15 to November 30, in a bid to ensure adequate supplies at reasonable prices during the festival season.

Dealers will be allowed to hold stock for only 15 days. The amended norms will not apply to Kolkata and its extended metropolitan areas, and Assam, where the limit is 2,000 quintals, the Food Ministry said in a statement.

The new sugar season began on October 1.

“By restricting the quantity and storage period of sugar, the government aims to facilitate the orderly movement of sugar through the supply chain and ensure its continuous availability to consumers at reasonable prices,” the Ministry said in a statement.

Kolkata buys sugar from Uttar Pradesh, Maharashtra, and Karnataka, and supplies it to eastern India, including the northeast. The limit for Assam takes into account geographical constraints, transportation facilities and consumer interest in the northeast, the Ministry said.

The Ministry said that the objective of the amended rules was to “ensure that there is no unnecessary accumulation of sugar in the distribution chain” and that the supply of sugar from mills through dealers to the consumer remained “smooth”.

In August, citing a tight supply year, the government had imposed a nationwide stock-holding limit on dealers of 4,000 quintals, applicable from August 1 to November 30, along with a maximum holding period of 30 days from the date of receipt. The limit was later tightened to 2,000 quintals from September 15.

According to the Ministry, average retail sugar prices have fallen 15% from their August peak and are expected to decline further as lower prices in the supply chain are realised. Ex-mill prices have dropped by around 28% and have remained stable for the past three weeks.

The government reiterated that mills, dealers, wholesalers and other market participants must ensure uninterrupted movement of sugar and prevent hoarding and speculation. Wholesalers and retailers have also been urged to “immediately pass on” the benefits of the sharp fall in ex-mill prices to consumers.

Sugar mills have been advised to begin crushing operations in line with agro-climatic conditions in their areas. State governments have also been asked to take appropriate action on crushing based on prevailing circumstances.

The Centre will continue to monitor the impact of erratic and inadequate rainfall linked to El Niño conditions on sugarcane in some producing areas, and will take timely measures to balance domestic availability, consumer interest and the interests of cane farmers, the Ministry said.

World.title: Chennai traffic police hold helmet awareness rally
World.content:
The Greater Chennai Traffic Police conducted a helmet awareness rally on Thursday. The rally was launched by Deputy Commissioner of Police, Traffic East District, S. Megalina Eden, on Sivananda Salai. Students from three colleges, traffic wardens, and traffic police personnel participated.

Ms. Eden said road accidents had declined compared with last year, mainly due to awareness programmes led by the police, greater public awareness, greater compliance with helmet rules among two-wheeler riders, strict enforcement, and fines issued based on automatic number plate recognition camera footage.

She said the ongoing Metro Rail and flyover works led to traffic congestion, particularly on Anna Salai in Saidapet and Teynampet. Traffic movement is expected to improve significantly, once these works are completed. “We are taking measures to ease traffic congestion on the OMR and ECR by deploying additional personnel at key points and regulating traffic flow,” she said.

World.title: Visakhapatnam’s Mahatma Gandhi hospital records 500 robotic cancer surgeries
World.content:
The Mahatma Gandhi Cancer Hospital & Research Institute (MGCHRI) announced that it has completed over 500 robotic cancer surgeries marking a significant milestone in precision oncology for the region.

Speaking to reporters on Thursday, Dr. Murali Krishna Voonna, Managing Director and Chief Surgical Oncologist, noted that crossing the milestone reflects the institution’s ongoing dedication to patient-centric, advanced medical care.

“Since establishing our dedicated robotic surgery unit, we have combined surgical precision with multidisciplinary expertise so patients can access high-quality cancer care closer to home,” he said.

These included a robotic left adrenalectomy for a patient presenting with severe hypertension due to a pheochromocytoma, and a delicate retroperitoneal lymph node dissection to excise a residual mass following chemotherapy for testicular cancer.

Clinicians emphasised that the enhanced visualisation and instrument control offered by robotic platforms are vital when operating within confined anatomical spaces near major blood vessels.

World.title: Tamil Nadu to get four more weather radars in next few years: IMD
World.content:
Tamil Nadu is set to get four more weather radars in the next few years. The State government plans to invest in radar network with technical support of India Meteorological Department (IMD), said Mrutyunjay Mohapatra, IMD Director General, here on Thursday.

Speaking on the sidelines of the Northeast monsoon seasonal outlook forum hosted jointly by IMD and the State government, he said the IMD would establish new radars at Tiruchi, Kanniyakumari, Yercaud, and Ramanathapuram to strengthen the observation network. Similarly, automatic rain gauges and automatic weather stations are being installed with IMD technical support, and the data generated would help assess hazards at the village level with accurate prediction. The forecast accuracy would further improve by 10% in the next three years.

Noting that the forecast accuracy has increased since 2021, he said IMD is now providing spatial probability forecast, indicating areas likely to get above or below average rainfall.

Heavy rainfall warning accuracy has improved by 40-50% in the past decade. Lightning and thunderstorms warning accuracy in nowcast is now 91%. Prediction of tropical cyclones, their landfall, and time has improved to almost nil error in recent years and reduced the loss of lives. Heatwave prediction accuracy stood at 88%.

Mr. Mohapatra said Northeast monsoon this year is likely to set in between October 15 and October 21 and Southwest monsoon may withdraw completely by October 15. On the relationship between El-Nino and rainfall over Tamil Nadu, he said the strong relationship observed before 2000, when strong El-Nino conditions were associated with good rainfall, had weakened over the last two decades. The State could receive normal rainfall during strong El-Nino years, he said.

Overall, the State is expected to get normal monsoon rainfall this year and the northern districts would experience normal to below normal rainfall. During El-Nino years, cyclones tend to have lower frequency and intensity, and a shorter track. However, cyclone can form over southeast Bay of Bengal and move west-northwestwards, he added.

This year, there is a high probability of systems moving towards Tamil Nadu, Puducherry, south Andhra Pradesh, and Sri Lanka coast. However, weather models do not provide forecasts of cyclone genesis frequency or intensity in the long-range forecast. Such cyclone forecasts are given two weeks in advance, he said.

World.title: ‘Why the need for all this drama’: DG ISPR lampoons India's 'neutralised Pakistani terrorist' claims, presents him before media
World.content:
Inter-Services Public Relations (ISPR) Director General Lt Gen Ahmed Sharif Chaudhry lampooned India’s claims of “neutralising” a “terrorist” allegedly linked to the Pakistani military, presenting the individual during a press conference on Thursday.

The press briefing came after Indian media reported that an individual wanted in connection with the April 22 Pahalgam terrorist attack last year had been killed during an “encounter” in Indian Illegally Occupied Kashmir’s Korag area.

Addressing the media, the DG ISPR said he would talk “about a so-called terrorist incident, a false flag that has been staged by the Indian political military”.

He presented a five-point timeline, showing that the whole scenario began on Sept 29.

“On the night of Sep 29, the Indian corps deployed in IIOK made a tweet, claiming that, based on joint intelligence reports, the Indian Army, police and CRPF launched an operation in general area of Korag, Yousmarg,” he read from a social media post by Chinar Corps.

The DG ISPR then referred to another post by Chinar Corps on Sept 30 morning that claimed the Indian forces had found the body of a “Lashkar-e-Taiba terrorist”.

The military spokesperson noted that later, India’s ANI news outlet claimed that the deceased had been identified as Mohammad Asif, who had been inducted into the Special Services Group (SSG).

The DG ISPR went on to say that India’s home affairs ministry and Press Information Bureau also reiterated the narrative.

India’s home affairs ministry said the neutralisation of “Musa alias Asif Fauji” was part of an “ongoing long-sustained Operation Sheruwali” that was launched in May.

“After six months of hard work, Musa alias Asif Fauji has been neutralised. Congratulations, applause,” Lt Gen Chaudhry retorted.

He then read out India’s claims of Asif’s so-called involvement in various attacks: “Halan attack August 23, DKG attack December 23, Kandi attack May 2023, Shah Sitar attack May 2024, Shiv Khori attack June 2024, Gagangeer attack October 2024, Boota Pahari attack October 2024, and Basira attack April 2025.”

The DG ISPR then noted that the Indian government also claimed to have neutralised three other “members of the group”.

“After this [press conference], the shameful characters will have at least the shame to delete this,” he remarked.

The DG ISPR also read out the Indian PIB’s narrative, which said their forces had killed “four senior LeT commanders”.

He took a jibe at Indian media too for highlighting the claims: “Now they said, ‘Let’s jump in’.

“So there comes News18, Statesman, India Today, Hindustan Times, ABP Live, Indian Express,” he said, as he displayed the screengrabs of these outlets’ reports on the matter.

The DG ISPR then called Asif to join him during the presser, who said he was a resident of Attock district.

“So here is that superman. You can see this superman. Please, come, my brother. Tell us about these achievements of yours, what all you have been doing,” Lt Gen Chaudhry quipped.

‘Here, alive and healthy’

Speaking before the media, Asif narrated: “Yesterday, some friends called me and told me there were reports on social media that I had been martyred by the Indian army in Kashmir.

“To their concerns, I responded that I was here, alive and healthy.”

Journalists at the ISPR press conference break into a laugh when Mohammad Asif, whom India claimed was killed in an oepration, appeared before them on Oct 1, 2026. — PTV News

Asif said he also received calls from Indian numbers, asking him for his personal information, identity, whereabouts and his connection with the claims.

“Through ANI on social media, I became aware of the reports that Indian media, using my personal data, had named me as a martyr in an operation in Kashmir,” Asif said.

“I was surprised by whatever was happening as I was sitting in my home,” he remarked.

Following the reports, Asif said that he informed his unit about the reports to clarify his position, and the unit asked him to block all the numbers calling from India and said that ISPR officials would contact him.

Sharing details about himself, Asif said that he joined the Pakistan Army in the year 2000. “In 2005, I joined the SSG, performed my duty with courage for 18 years, and retired in 2023.”

Asif added that he had also worked for a private security company for three years. “For the past three or four months, I have been living with my family in our home in Rawalpindi.”

He termed the Indian allegations as “false, ignominious and disreputable”.

“I condemn this. By the grace of God, I am alive and present before you.“

He further affirmed that he performed his duties with courage and that Pakistan responds face to face, not from behind.

‘Six reasons behind such dramas’

Five of the six “reasons” listed by ISPR DG Lt Gen Ahmed Sharif Chaudhry for what he said were India’s false flag operations. — screengrab via PTV News

Taking on the mic, the DG ISPR maintained that there were “six reasons” behind “such dramas” by India against Pakistan.

“It is a very shameful and embarrassing thing. No self-respecting nation does this.”

‘Cover own track of terrorism’

Explaining the first reason, Lt Gen Chaudhry said that India did those theatrics to “cover its own track of terrorism”. “So, there has to be some good reason,” he added.

“India is the biggest sponsor of terrorism and a terrorist state in the world,“ the DG ISPR declared.

“And its implication, involvement, direct and indirect terrorism in the region goes back decades,” he added.

“Whether it’s Mukti Bahini or LTT, and now the TTP, BLA, and their funding, sponsorship and planning. It (India) has now become a victim of its own trait.”

The military spokesperson highlighted that this terrorism was also “now taking on an internal dimension”.

He elaborated: “They are not just terrorising the region or countries around the region; they are terrorising the Muslims inside India, and also the Kashmiris, Sikhs, Dalits, Christians, [residents of] Manipur, and tribals.

“Some country which lives and breathes terrorism is at the same time very afraid that their dark face will be exposed, so they have to cover their tracks. What better way to cover their tracks than to start calling everyone else a terrorist?”

Lt Gen Chaudhry then played a video clip on the “decades of lies that they have been feeding to their own people as well as to the world at large”.

He accused India of jailing Muslim Kashmiris, adding: “They take them out, kill them, and stage that as a false flag operation, portraying it as a terrorist act.”

The DG ISPR quipped: “This time they went ahead; they said this is not very spicy, let’s take an army soldier of Pakistan and portray him as one that we have killed.”

He then brought attention to India’s involvement in transnational killings, saying, “This habit of false flag operations has further encouraged India to go for transnational killings.”

He added, “Everyone whom they don’t like, they start calling terrorists, because they see their image.”

The military spokesperson then played a video containing a clip of an Afghan minister saying “our DNA is one” as he referred to India.

“That is the illegitimate child of this terrorism, which is on our western border,” Lt Gen Chaudhry said, referring to Afghanistan.

“Because what better opportunity than to give this dirty work to someone who is ready to do it for certain coins and dollars and money,” he retorted.

A soundbite by Afghan Agriculture Minister Mawlawi Attaullah Omari is played during a press conference held by Inter-Services Public Relations Director General Lt Gen Ahmed Sharif Chaudhry on Oct 1, 2026. — DawnNewsTV

‘Oppression in occupied Kashmir’

The DG ISPR then identified the second reason for the claims as the developments in occupied Jammu and Kashmir, describing it as the “biggest garrison of the world”.

“What’s happening in Indian Illegally Occupied Jammu and Kashmir plays a big role in the psyche and in the cognitive domain of these Indians,” he asserted.

“For every 10th Kashmiri, there is an Indian soldier or a security person. There are nearly 1 million military, security, and intelligence CRPF and law enforcement there,” he pointed out, noting other acts such as arrests and demolition of houses.

“And you cannot subside them; you cannot take out their desire to be counted. It’s a simple desire,” Lt Gen Chaudhry said, noting that Kashmiris wanted the right of self-determination as promised in a United Nations Security Council resolution.

He stated that New Delhi had to stage such incidents to “portray that Kashmiris have no problem”, whereas the reality was otherwise due to the “oppression” being committed against them.

“You have an internal problem, a great internal problem of oppression, of torture. [But] you don’t want to address it; you want to externalise it. You cannot externalise your internal issues. You cannot put this blame on Muhammad Asif.”

‘Obsession with Pakistan’

The third reason, the DG ISPR said, was India’s “obsession with Pakistan”.

He remarked: “I think Pakistan, over a period of time, has got on their nerves so much that whatever happens, they want to put it on Pakistan.

“And therefore, their politico-military leadership imagination and faculties have somehow been constrained and restricted. […] And that’s why we keep on requesting them very politely, asking them, please grow up.”

The military spokesperson, as in May last year, urged India to come forward with evidence if it had any behind its claims and allegations.

“If you are not ready to give proof to us, you can give it to any third party,” he offered.

‘Bollywood influence’

Lt Gen Chaudhry stated that the fourth reason was New Delhi being “very much influenced” by Bollywood, adding that “they have turned into encounter-istan from Hindustan”.

“It is the story that is important; the facts are not important to Indians,” he said, declaring claims by India and its media as “fiction”.

He quipped that for India, the “story should be clear, the story should be spicy”.

“There should be action in it; it should be entertaining […] make the encounter look real, throw in a Pakistani — just an ordinary Pakistani won’t be fun, let’s put in a havaldar, let’s put in an SSG guard, then it will be thrilling.”

‘Shining India delusion’

Fifth reason, as per the DG ISPR, was a “delusional ‘Shining India’ complex” that the neighbour had.

“They think that they are great,” he said, recalling the field marshal’s remarks that “they are great without greatness”.

“They are historical without history, and the shine — this is the shine that you are seeing. It is not shine; it is shame,” he remarked, contending that India presumed it could “control the mind” of others in the world like it controls its media.

‘Politicisation of military’

At last, the military spokesperson explained that the “politicisation” of the Indian military was another reason behind such tactics.

“We cannot comprehend that we would be able to come out with such a story and such claims which don’t exist,“ he said.

He asserted that the Indian brigade, corps commander and army commander allowed this and took responsibility for it “because you are a political army now”.

“Your [Indian Army] agenda is Hindutva-driven. Your agenda is pleasing your political masters.”

Lt Gen Chaudhry added, “Unfortunately, we have to deal with such a wretched and low-life kind of enemy. It is unfortunate that we have such a neighbour who is an encounter specialist.

“[…] This is what the world, Pakistan, particularly the region, and the world at large is facing.”

India warned of ‘very harsh retribution’

Asked about whether the recent allegations could trigger another armed conflict between the neighbours, the DG ISPR affirmed that Pakistan’s armed forces were always ready for any such move and warned of a “very harsh” retribution.

“As a consequence of this false flag, which has been exposed very early in its infancy, if they want to do anything, most welcome.

“[…] But let it be clear, and we have clarified it before also, that this time we will not leave them so easily. This time the cost that Pakistan would inflict on their strategic folly will be very, very severe.”

He reiterated, “If they think that they want to build this drama, any other drama, and on the basis of that they want to do it, they can try their luck.”

He also disputed the impression that the international community had a lack of response to India’s transnational killings. While noting that the Foreign Office (FO) could give a more nuanced reply, he said, “I think the Indian facade is very well exposed to the whole world.”

Lt Gen Chaudhry recalled that a US secretary of state, former Canadian prime minister Justin Trudeau, and Australian leaders were among those who had raised their concerns about such killings.

Responding to another query, the DG ISPR said India was “unreliable” and a “country which believes in deceit, terrorism and which believes in having their own hegemony in the region”.

“So, the only guarantee of peace against such a country is our own strength.”

Asked about the current status of Indian spy Kulbhushan Jadhav, who was captured in Balochistan in March 2016, the military spokesman said the law ministry was the relevant forum to approach.

“Whether he is alive or dead, it is smeared on India’s face and will remain so.”

Responding to other questions, the DG ISPR also reaffirmed Pakistan’s right to self-defence against terror attacks emanating from Afghanistan, as well as declared that the counterterror fight “cannot be sacrificed at the altar of anyone’s politics”.

Indian media’s claims

Indian media had claimed that the supposedly slain individual was affiliated with the banned LeT and was a soldier of the Pakistan military. The claim, attributed to “sources”, named the individual as Mohammad Asif.

It may be recalled that Indian media and authorities had made several allegations regarding Pakistani involvement in the April 2025 Pahalgam incident, but failed to substantiate them.

“Mohammad Asif alias Hashim Moosa was born on 07 March 1980. He joined the Pakistan Army in 2000 under service number PA-3106947 and retired with the rank of Havildar,” India’s ANI reported on Thursday.

It also provided a detailed profile of Asif.

“In 2005, Mohammad Asif was inducted into the Special Services Group (SSG). He served with 4 Commando ‘Yalgar’ Battalion and was posted to Balochistan from 2006 onward. During his deployment in Balochistan, he reportedly participated in approximately 10 operations against Baloch insurgents and is credited with 13 personal kills,” the ANI news report stated, adding that Asif was also part of the security detail of former president Pervez Musharraf.

It was stated by ANI that Asif was “wanted in the Pahalgam terror attack”, and the claim was repeated by the Indian Army’s Chinar Corps — part of the Northern Command and headquartered in occupied Kashmir. The corps primary area of responsibility is the Kashmir area of operations.

In May 2025, a four-day conflict between Pakistan and India was sparked by an attack on tourists in occupied Kashmir’s Pahalgam, which New Delhi, without evidence, linked to Pakistan.

Islamabad had strongly denied responsibility while calling for a neutral investigation .

After New Delhi launched deadly air strikes in Punjab and Azad Kashmir on May 7, Pakistan said it downed at least six Indian aircraft in air-to-air combat, later raising the tally to eight .

After tit-for-tat strikes on each other’s airbases, it took American intervention on May 10 for both sides to finally reach a ceasefire .

During that conflict, Indian media had been heavily criticised for beating the war drums and regurgitating fake news fed by Indian government sources. Many mainstream Indian channels had also aired inflammatory anti-Pakistan and anti-Muslim content.

India’s ranking in the Reporters Without Borders’ World Press Freedom Index has deteriorated sharply over the past decade. The country ranked 122nd in 2010 but fell to 157th out of 180 countries in 2026.

In April, on the first anniversary of the Pahalgam attack, Pakistan had rejected a renewed Indian propaganda campaign linking it to the attack, deploring that the neighbouring country was focusing on “weaponising its false narrative” in the midst of a regional crisis sparked by the US-Israel war on Iran.

World.title: PM Shehbaz met Trump at reception banquet on UNGA sidelines
World.content:
Prime Minister Shehbaz Sharif met United States President Donald Trump during the reception banquet hosted by the latter in honour of world leaders, on the sidelines of the 81st session of the United Nations General Assembly (UNGA) in New York last month, according to details released by the Press Information Department (PID) on Thursday.

The PID shared photographs, released by the White House, of the two leaders standing together, smiling and shaking hands.

No further details about the interaction were provided.

The UNGA debate ran from Sept 22 to 26, with a final sitting on Sept 28. PM Shehbaz addressed the session on Sept 25 and was also mentioned by US President Donald Trump in his speech, who called him a “terrific man”. The premier also held bilateral meetings on the sidelines of the UNGA with world leaders, including Iranian President Masoud Pezeshkian.

The premier’s official visit to New York, him meeting Trump and his participation in the UNGA debate came as Pakistan plays the role of a mediator for de-escalation between the US and Iran.

Earlier this year, PM Shehbaz and Trump were also together at the signing of the charter for the “ Board of Peace ” — which has been constituted primarily to provide a roadmap to end the Israeli assault in Gaza — in January.

Then, they also met at the inaugural meeting of the Board of Peace in Washington, DC in February.

State-run APP reported that an informal meeting was held between the two at the end of the summit.

During the interaction, the two leaders expressed mutual goodwill and shook hands, the APP report said, adding that the US president also embraced PM Shehbaz.

The premier had also met with Trump, alongside other world leaders, at a ceremony following the signing of a ceasefire agreement between Israel and Hamas at the Sharm el-Sheikh Peace Summit in Egypt in October 2025.

The two leaders had met for the first time at the Oval Office in Washington on September 25, 2025 in which they discussed regional security and cooperation among other matters. This was also around a UNGA session.

The premier was accompanied by Chief of Defence Forces and Chief of the Army Staff Field Marshal Asim Munir, while the US president was joined by Vice President JD Vance and Secretary of State Marco Rubio.

The two sides had discussed regional security and cooperation along the lines of counter-terrorism, among other matters.

World.title: Saudi-led coalition says Houthis attacked power station in Madina
World.content:
The Saudi-led coalition fighting Yemen’s Houthis said on Thursday the group had attacked a power distribution station in Madina this week, putting one transformer out of service but without affecting the electricity network.

The coalition said an investigation and examination of drone wreckage confirmed Houthi involvement in planning and carrying out Tuesday’s attack. It said the station supplies electricity to the Prophet’s Mosque.

A Houthi military source, quoted by the Houthi-run Saba news agency, denied the accusation, calling it a “lie” and saying it was intended to cover up what he described as Saudi Arabia’s failure to substantiate its earlier accusation that the Houthis targeted Makkah.

Saudi Arabia said two weeks ago it had intercepted and destroyed a Houthi drone south of Makkah before it entered restricted airspace over the city. The coalition described that incident as the second Houthi attempt to target Makkah since 2017, while the Houthis denied targeting Makkah or any other Islamic holy site.

The coalition said the Madina attack was part of what it described as repeated Houthi attempts to target the Two Holy Mosques and “provoke” Muslims worldwide. It said it would continue taking measures to protect the holy sites and pilgrims.

The latest escalation is the most serious fighting between Saudi Arabia and the Houthis since a UN-brokered truce largely halted cross-border attacks in 2022. Hostilities resumed this year after the Houthis declared a naval blockade on Saudi Arabia in July and began attacking Saudi territory and shipping, while Houthi forces also made major territorial gains along Yemen’s Red Sea coast.

Saudi Arabia has responded with airstrikes in Yemen and backed government forces fighting to push back the Houthis.

World.title: PPP to join govt representatives as Shehbaz-Zardari meeting yields Friday talks with opposition
World.content:
A joint delegation of the PPP and the government would hold a meeting with the PTI leadership on Friday, identical statements released by the PPP and the Presidency said.

The decision was taken after Prime Minister Shehbaz Sharif called on President Asif Ali Zardari at Aiwan-i-Sadr in Islamabad.

The statement said “current political situation” in the country would be discussed with the opposition on Friday, adding that President Zardari and PM Shehbaz review the national security situation and stressed the need for effective cooperation between relevant institutions for peace and stability in the country.

The development comes as the PTI’s planned Oct 4 march to Islamabad remains a source of contention between the opposition party and the Centre.

A source told Dawn that possibility of imposing emergency in Khyber Pakhtunkhwa — where the PTI is in power — was also discussed at the huddle at the Presidency, but it was agreed that the government should first give the opposition “a chance to settle issues through dialogue and in a peaceful manner”.

However, it was also agreed that if the opposition did not abandon its plan for the march, the “government will seriously think about imposing emergency in the KP”.

PTI Chairperson Barrister Gohar Khan also confirmed that a meeting between opposition and government representatives would be held on Friday.

“PTI Chairman Barrister Gohar Khan received a message from the government yesterday for a meeting, which he has accepted in light of the decisions made in today’s opposition meeting. God willing, a meeting will take place between the opposition and government delegations in the office of National Assembly Speaker Sardar Ayaz Sadiq tomorrow at 12pm,” a post on Gohar’s X account said.

According to the PPP statement, Interior Minister Mohsin Naqvi, Adviser to the PM on Political Affairs Rana Sanaullah, PPP Senator Sherry Rehman and PPP MNAs Naveed Qamar and Aijaz Jakhrani would participate in the meeting.

From the opposition’s side, opposition alliance Tehreek-i-Tahaffuz Ayeen-i-Pakistan (TTAP) spokesperson Akhundzada Yousafzai also confirmed his, as well as Senate Opposition Leader Allama Raja Nasir Abbas and former senator Mustafa Nawaz Khokhar’s participation.

However, National Assembly Opposition Leader Mehmood Khan Achakzai and TTAP chairman has ruled out his participation at any meeting in the speaker’s chamber.

A senior TTAP leader further told Dawn that even Abbas was unwilling to visit the speaker’s chamber for the meeting but had agreed to participate at the PTI’s request.

The opposition alliance’s decision came after a meeting with PTI leaders in the Senate opposition leader’s chamber.

Discussion at the meeting covered the overall political situation in the country, PTI’s planned protest march and other constitutional and parliamentary matters, a statement by the TTAP said.

The possibility of a meeting between government and opposition representative is being seen as a means to defuse the current political crisis in the country, with the PTI’s planned Oct 4 protest march to demand Imran’s release becoming the new bone of contention between the party and the Centre.

As the PTI remains resolute to go ahead with the march, federal ministers have warned that the Centre would have no other option but to impose the governor’s rule or emergency in KP in light of the security situation in the province and the PTI’s protest call on Oct 4.

For its part, the opposition party has warned the government of dire consequences if such a decision is imposed.

The TTAP, which is headed by Achakzai and also includes the PTI, has announced that it would join the protest.

‘Anywhere but not at PM Office, speaker’s chamber’

After the TTAP-PTI meeting, Achakzai said he was not ready to hold parleys at the Prime Minister’s House or Office or the Speaker’s Chamber.

“The prime minister is illegitimate. The mandate of millions of Pakistanis … Harsh words are rising to my lips; that is why I am silent.

“I am ready to sit anywhere in Pakistan, under any tree. I am ready to visit the house of any party [leader]. But I will not go to the speaker house [sic], the Prime Minister’s House or the prime minister’s chamber,” he said while speaking to the media at Parliament House after the opposition leaders’ meeting, standing alongside Gohar.

Achakzai’s remarks were in response to a question about the prime minister’s adviser, Rana Sanaullah, inviting him and PTI Chairperson Barrister Gohar to hold a sitting with the premier. The reporter asked him why the meeting was not taking place.

In a video clip shared by the opposition alliance Tehreek-i-Tahaffuz Ayeen-i-Pakistan (TTAP), Achakzai also said the meeting with the prime minister would take place after a meeting with jailed former premier and PTI founder Imran Khan.

PM Shehbaz had extended an invitation to the NA opposition leader to sit together for consultations on the issues of national impor­tance and those related to the PTI before leaving for the US. Earlier, the premier also invited Achakzai on Sept 11 for mandatory consultation on the appointment of a new chief election commi­ssioner.

Gohar’s warning against imposition of emergency

For his part, Barrister Gohar told the media that PTI leaders had held a three-hour meeting with Abbas and Achakzai in which they had a detailed exchange of views on the problems facing the country and the current situation, particularly in KP and regarding the march preparations.

He condemned the “state oppression and tyranny” inflicted on the PTI and its supporters, as well as the detention and treatment of Imran’s sisters in jail.

The PTI chairman claimed that attempts were made to suppress his party “whenever we raise our voice for our rights and for justice in the country”.

Gohar also stressed that the party had “always stood with the state and the country”, including during the May 2025 conflict with India.

Gohar added that the leaders had also discussed reports regarding the potential imposition of emergency and warned: “The federation becomes strong when the provinces are strong and autonomous, and when the people’s mandate is respected. You will put the federation at risk if you take any action in a province that goes against the will of its people.”

He reiterated that the PTI’s march would remain peaceful, saying, “This is our country; for us, Pakistan comes first, the state of Pakistan and its peace and security.”

The PTI chairman stated that the way to avoid a long march was not by the imposition of governor’s rule or a state of emergency, but rather by talking to protesters, listening to the purpose for which they were out on the streets, and addressing their concerns.

“We went to the Supreme Court 19 times, but were not heard. We went to the high court 25 times but its orders were not implemented. A special committee was formed in Parliament, but a meeting was never called … Even today, the same concerns persist,” he said.

Gohar stressed that despite all this, the party was ready for negotiations and had made their demands clear before everyone.

PTI Secretary General Salman Akram Raja also stressed that protesting was a constitutional and legal right, and the party would not back down from their protest.

“The leader of the long march is Sohail Afridi; Imran Khan has appointed him. We will support him in every possible way,” he added.

‘Opposition ready for dialogue but without conditions’

Speaking to the media alongside Achakzai and Gohar after the meeting in his chamber, Senate Opposition Leader Abbas called for reconciliation and dialogue to resolve the country’s political crisis, saying his side was ready for talks, but without preconditions.

He also stressed that the PTI’s protest would be peaceful even when met with violence, and that “no false narrative” should be created against the protest.

“I have said before as well that when we leave from there, there will be no weapons in our hands,” he said. “We know the value of human life.”

Abbas called for a move towards reconciliation and dialogue in order to improve the country’s situation.

“We are fully prepared to hold dialogue and correct the situation, but this will be without any conditions. If anyone thinks that they will hold a dagger of conditions at our necks, then, such a thing will never be accepted,” he said.

Regarding the proposed protest, Abbas said the PTI had “decided to adopt a democratic approach by staging peaceful protests and a long march”.

He said the government should have “assured the protesters of the protection of their lives and property, provided them with facilities, and, while recognising the right to peaceful protest, designated the routes”.

“But, on the contrary, what did the government do? Even before the protests began, containers were placed to seal Islamabad, roads were dug up and nails were hammered into the routes,” he said, claiming that this was the behaviour of “scared people”.

Stressing that the Constitution guaranteed the rights of the Pakistani people, Abbas said peaceful protests, sit-ins and long marches were part of democratic politics.

The opposition leader also criticised the reported arrests of PTI members under the Maintenance of Public Order law, terming it a completely “illegal practice”.

On Imran, Abbas said, “The only personality who can take Pakistan out of the current crisis is Imran Khan, whom the people trust.”

“He will go to Balochistan, where Akhtar Mengal and other leaders will be with him. He will sit with the people and talk to them and convince them. What you cannot do through the force of bullets can be done through dialogue because the people trust him,” he added.

In the morning, Adviser to the Prime Minister on Political Affairs Rana Sanaullah said that the federal government and PTI had been engaged in “off-the-record talks” regarding PTI’s planned protest on Oct 4.

Sanaullah made the remarks while appearing in Geo News’ morning show “Geo Pakistan”.

Sanaullah said that the decision on the proposed march rested with PTI’s senior leadership, “with whom off-the-record consultation is ongoing”.

“So let us see, even if they do not postpone it, we have arrangements in place to stop them,” Sanaullah warned.

He likened the PTI’s march to a “provincial government attacking the capital” in an apparent reference to the PTI-led government in KP.

“If a political party or a private organisation stages a protest, […] but for a government to attack […] it cannot be tolerated under any circumstances,” he held.

“The law will be enacted in full force, and they (PTI) will be barred from entering Islamabad,” he added.

Responding to a question about governor’s rule in Khyber Pakhtunkhwa, Sanaullah on Thursday said that the option was “on the table”.

Sanaullah further clarified that the federal government was in talks with coalition parties about imposing governor’s rule in KP. He added that the final decision rested upon the federal government and the Senate, adding that it would only come into effect with parliament’s approval.

Sanaullah alleged that the KP chief minister had not been performing his functions as the province’s chief executive.

“For the past two months, he has not done anything, nothing about development or counter-terrorism efforts or for the welfare of people […] in fact, all he has done is talk about marching to Islamabad and toppling the federal government.

“They want to take ladders to Islamabad to secure the release of a certain someone,” he added.

Sanaullah reiterated that if a province is “engaged in such illegal and unconstitutional activities, then the Centre has the right to declare emergency or governor rule and assume power”.

Additional reporting by Ikram Junaidi and Irfan Raza

World.title: Govt raises petrol price by Rs3.26 per litre, reduces high-speed diesel rate by Rs1.01 per litre
World.content:
The government on Thursday raised the price of petrol by Rs3.26 per litre, but reduced that of high-speed diesel (HSD) by Rs1.01 per litre.

Following the revision, petrol will retail at Rs390.66 per litre, while HSD will cost Rs399.34 per litre. The government continues to levy Rs114 per litre in taxes and duties on petrol and Rs100 per litre on diesel.

According to the Petroleum Division’s notification, the new prices are applicable for Oct 2 (Friday).

The price of HSD has come down from a peak of Rs520.35 recorded on April 3. Its price had started rising from Rs281 per litre after the US-Iran war broke out on February 28.

The petrol price had peaked at Rs458.41 on April 3 after beginning its upward trajectory from Rs266 in the first week of March.

Meanwhile, the government has reintroduced a raft of austerity measures in response to rising fuel prices amid the ongoing Middle East conflict. Under these measures, markets are required to close by 9pm and fuel allocations for official vehicles has been cut by 50 per cent for three months.

On September 13, Prime Minister Shehbaz Sharif also announced a “ relief scheme ” for users of motorcycles, autos and vehicles of up to 800cc to “alleviate the burden” of rising global oil prices.

Deputy Prime Minister and Foreign Minister Ishaq Dar on Sept 29 appreciated the success of the scheme , saying that it reflected a “whole of government” approach.

Chairing a meeting of the National Steering Committee on Fuel Subsidy to review the implementation of the scheme, the deputy premier noted that the information, IT and petroleum ministries, as well as the Oil and Gas Regulatory Authority (Ogra), the State Bank of Pakistan (SBP) and all provinces, had made “concerted” efforts for the scheme.

It was noted that to date, around 7.60 million registrations have been successfully made, and the token redemption process has entered the second week. Moreover, 7.71m tokens have been redeemed.

Previously, on July 17, Petroleum Minister Ali Pervaiz Malik announced that fuel prices would now be fixed on a daily basis due to fluctuations in international market prices following renewed hostilities between Iran and the US.

Prior to this, the government had been announcing weekly revisions to fuel prices since early March, alongside measures for the conservation of fuel amid possible oil supply disruptions due to the ongoing conflict in the Middle East. The federal government in April also announced targeted relief measures to provide subsidised fuel.

The petroleum minister stated that the cabinet and the prime minister had decided to give the Oil and Gas Regulatory Authority (Ogra) the responsibility of deciding fuel prices on a daily basis based on international market trends.

Petrol is mainly used in private transport, small vehicles, rickshaws and two-wheelers, and changes in its price affect the middle and lower-middle classes.

Similarly, changes in diesel prices also impact the public at large, as it is mainly used in the heavy transport sector, power plants and large generators.

Petrol and high-speed diesel (HSD) are the major revenue earners, with monthly sales of about 700,000 to 800,000 tonnes, compared to just 10,000 tonnes of monthly demand for kerosene.

World.title: Pakistan, India and Australia in same 2027 Cricket World Cup group
World.content:
India will meet defending champions Australia and bitter rivals Pakistan in their first two matches at the 2027 Cricket World Cup, the International Cricket Council announced on Thursday.

The India-Australia match, a repeat of the 2023 final, will be in Cape Town on October 7 and the India-Pakistan clash will take place in Johannesburg three days later.

The tournament, hosted by South Africa, Zimbabwe and Namibia, will start on October 4 and the final will be played on November 27.

The group match between India and Pakistan will be played at the Wanderers Stadium, the tournament’s biggest venue and tickets are almost certain to be in high demand.

After a preliminary round to eliminate two of the three lowest-ranked teams, 12 teams will be split into two groups for round-robin matches before the top three in each group, and the best fourth-placed team, qualify for a Super Seven phase, followed by semi-finals and the final.

Because of political tensions between the two countries, India and Pakistan have only played each other in ICC events since Pakistan toured India for three One-day Internationals and two Twenty20 internationals in December 2012.

The rivalry is intense despite India having won all eight matches against Pakistan in Cricket World Cups and eight out of nine in T20 World Cups.

Afghanistan, Zimbabwe and a qualifier will also be in Group ‘A’.

World.title: Fight against terrorism is 'paramount', cannot be 'sacrificed at altar of anyone’s politics': DG ISPR
World.content:
Inter-Services Public Relations (ISPR) Director General Lt Gen Ahmed Sharif Chaudhry on Thursday declared that Pakistan’s fight against terrorism was “paramount” and could not be “sacrificed at the altar of anyone’s politics”.

He was addressing a press conference to rebut India’s claims of neutralising an individual linked to the Pakistan Army in an “encounter” in the Korag area of India-occupied Kashmir.

Taking on a question regarding political leaders in Pakistan who advocated for negotiating with the Afghan Taliban over terrorism, he said different people could have different thoughts on how to counter the menace.

“There is no problem in it. We need to discuss, and we need to come, and we need to say that yes, this is how we need to go forward and fight this.”

The military spokesperson maintained that the fight against terrorism was an “enduring fight, and this has to be won”. “We will win it,” he asserted, saying there was no other choice.

The DG ISPR said Pakistan was the “largest victim of terrorism” as it had been battling it for more than two decades and had lost more than 100,000 people in the process, besides facing economic losses.

“More than this, our political and social fabric has suffered badly.”

He recalled that as a result of the debate surrounding Pakistan’s counter-terror fight, the political leadership drafted the National Action Plan (NAP), then revised it, and finally came up with the ‘Azm-i-Istehkam’ vision.

“These are the agreed consensual documents. You all and politicians have drafted them. Then follow them,” he emphasised.

Replying to the query, he said: “If there is terrorism in the region and if you create confusion in its narrative and don’t do capacity building, then the question comes: is this behaviour only incompetence, lack of understanding, indifference or willful collusion?

“These questions will arise because for us, the most important thing is: politics exists if the state does, democracy exists if the state does, you and I exist if the state does.”

Lt Gen Chaudhry said that Pakistan had an “existential threat from Indian-sponsored terrorism”.

He highlighted that the country’s police, intelligence, soldiers, and officers were fighting this war against terrorism on a daily basis.

“But then the other stakeholders, if they are not coming up, then the question is: why are you not fighting it? Why are you not standing [against it]? Are you doing it because you are a coward? Are you doing it because you are complicit?”

He further remarked that it was up to the people and government of Pakistan to “realise that”.

“This fight against terrorism is paramount. This cannot stop, this cannot be compromised, this cannot be sacrificed at the altar of anyone’s politics,” he asserted.

To another question regarding the PTI’s planned march to Islamabad on Oct 4, the DG ISPR said, “The army has got nothing to do with politics, and we will not answer anything about politics.

“I have made it repeatedly clear. Politics is for the political parties.”

World.title: Consumer inflation eases to 10.3pc in September from 11.1pc in August, official data shows
World.content:
ISLAMABAD: Consumer inflation eased to 10.3 per cent in September from 11.1pc a month earlier, mainly due to a sharp slowdown in food inflation, the Pakistan Bureau of Statistics said on Thursday.

The slight deceleration in the inflation rate, measured by the Consumer Price Index, reversed the sharp increase recorded in August, when higher food and energy prices pushed the annual rate to 11.1pc from 9.2pc in July.

The easing was more pronounced in rural areas, where inflation fell to 10.5pc from 12.2pc, while urban inflation edged down to 10.1pc from 10.4pc.

The September reading was also within the Ministry of Finance’s projection of 10pc to 11pc for the month in its Monthly Economic Update and Outlook for September 2026.

However, despite the decline in the annual rate, prices rose 1.3pc month-on-month in September. The annual inflation rate was 5.8pc in September last year.

The easing was largely driven by food prices. Food inflation dropped to 8.1pc in urban areas in September from 12.1pc in August. The decline was much sharper in rural areas, where food inflation fell to 7.7pc from 13.2pc a month earlier.

However, non-food inflation moved in the opposite direction, indicating continued pressure on household expenses. Urban non-food inflation accelerated to 11.5pc from 9.4pc in August, while rural non-food inflation increased to 13.1pc from 11.3pc.

The finance ministry had warned in its September 2026 outlook that inflationary pressures were concentrated in food and energy following the impact of higher global oil prices on domestic energy, transport and food costs.

In August, food, housing and utilities, and transport together contributed 8.2 percentage points, or about three-quarters of headline inflation. Food alone contributed 4.9 percentage points.

The latest data show that the composition of inflation shifted in September. While food inflation slowed sharply, electricity and transport costs continued to rise. Electricity charges increased by 15.28pc from the previous month, while motor fuel prices rose by 10.76pc in urban areas.

At the national level, transport costs increased by 5.75pc during September and were 27.43pc higher than in the same month last year. Housing, water, electricity, gas and fuels increased by 3.05pc during the month and by 12.39pc on an annual basis.

Core inflation, which excludes volatile food and energy components, also eased slightly. It stood at 8.6pc in urban areas in September, compared with 8.8pc in August, while the rural rate declined to 8.1pc from 8.5pc.
